source.text: Ἦν δὲ τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὰ ἄζυμα μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας.

records.literal_gloss: It was now the Passover and the Unleavened [Bread] after two days.

en.L: Now it was the Passover and the [Feast of] Unleavened Bread after two days.
en.B: Two days remained before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
en.R: In two more days it would be time for the Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread.

es.L: Y era la Pascua y [la fiesta de] los Panes sin Levadura después de dos días.
es.B: Faltaban dos días para la Pascua y la fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura.
es.R: Dentro de dos días iba a ser la Pascua y la fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura.

sw.L: Na ilikuwa Pasaka na [Sikukuu ya] Mikate Isiyo na Chachu baada ya siku mbili.
sw.B: Zilikuwa zimebaki siku mbili kabla ya Pasaka na Sikukuu ya Mikate Isiyo na Chachu.
sw.R: Baada ya siku mbili ingekuwa wakati wa Pasaka na Sikukuu ya Mikate Isiyo na Chachu.

decisions.choice: the Passover and Unleavened Bread: one festival week
decisions.reason: The Passover meal was eaten on the night of 15 Nisan and was followed by seven days of eating bread without yeast (Exodus 12:1-20; Leviticus 23:5-6). By this time the two names were used together for the whole festival.

decisions.choice: after two days: two days from now
alternatives: two full days later, on the third day
decisions.reason: The phrase counts forward from the time Mark is describing; it places the plot of 14:1-2 just before the feast.

decisions.choice: Festival of Unleavened Bread
decisions.reason: Readable uses "festival", an everyday word for a holy feast.

decisions.choice: los Panes sin Levadura
decisions.reason: The festival week of bread made without yeast that followed the Passover meal (meaning decision m1). "Ázimos" is the old liturgical word, unknown to most readers; "Panes sin Levadura" says what the feast was named for. The same in 14:12.

source.text: καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς πῶς αὐτὸν ἐν δόλῳ κρατήσαντες ἀποκτείνωσιν, ἔλεγον γάρ· Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, μήποτε ἔσται θόρυβος τοῦ λαοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And were seeking the chief priests and the scribes how him by deceit having seized they might kill. \v 2 They were saying for, Not during the feast, lest there will be an uproar of the people.

en.L: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by deceit [and] kill [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}]. \v 2 For they were saying, "Not during the feast, or there will be an uproar of the people."
en.B: The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by a trick and put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death. \v 2 For they kept saying, "Not at the feast, in case the people raise an uproar."
en.R: The leading priests and the teachers of God's law were trying to find a secret way to arrest Jesus and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 2 They said, "We must not do it during the festival. The crowds might start a riot."

es.L: Y los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas buscaban cómo, apoderándose de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} con engaño, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matarían. \v 2 Porque decían: «No durante la fiesta, no sea que haya alboroto del pueblo».
es.B: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas buscaban cómo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} podrían arrestar con una trampa y darle muerte. \v 2 Porque se decían: «Durante la fiesta no, no sea que el pueblo se alborote».
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los maestros de la ley buscaban una manera de arrestar a Jesús en secreto y matarlo. \v 2 Decían: «No debemos hacerlo durante la fiesta. La gente podría armar un alboroto».

sw.L: Na wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi walikuwa wakitafuta jinsi ya kumkamata kwa hila [na] kumuua. \v 2 Kwa maana walikuwa wakisema, "Si wakati wa sikukuu, isije ikatokea ghasia ya watu."
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi walikuwa wakitafuta njia ya kumkamata kwa hila ili wamuue. \v 2 Kwa maana walikuwa wakisemezana, "Tusifanye hivyo wakati wa sikukuu, watu wasije wakafanya fujo."
sw.R: Wakuu wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria walikuwa wakitafuta njia ya siri ya kumkamata Yesu na kumuua. \v 2 Walisema, "Tusifanye hivyo wakati wa sikukuu. Umati wa watu unaweza kuanzisha ghasia."

decisions.choice: by deceit: by a trick, out of public view
decisions.reason: The word means cunning or treachery. They want to seize Jesus quietly, away from the crowds who listened to him gladly (12:37).

decisions.choice: the feast: Passover week, when Jerusalem was full of pilgrims
alternatives: the meal on the first night only
decisions.reason: Large crowds came for the festival, and the Romans feared unrest at this time. An arrest in public could start a riot.

decisions.choice: they were saying: they kept saying among themselves
alternatives: they said it once in public
decisions.reason: The tense describes talk that went on while they made their plans.

decisions.choice: leading priests; teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: The same Readable terms as in earlier chapters.

decisions.choice: los jefes de los sacerdotes; los escribas (L, B), los maestros de la ley (R)
alternatives: los maestros de la ley at every level
decisions.reason: The terms used for these groups throughout Mark, recorded once in this chapter. Readable says what the scribes were, as the English "teachers of God's law" does.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns, pronouns before the verb and possessives (él, lo, le, su, mi, me, ti)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the end of the verb ("matarlo", "entregárselo"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani; waandishi (L, B), walimu wa sheria (R)
alternatives: walimu wa sheria at every level
decisions.reason: The terms used for these groups throughout Mark, recorded once in this chapter. Readable says what the scribes were, as the English "teachers of God's law" does.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yake, wangu, mimi, nami)
alternatives: a span wherever the English has one
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("kumkamata", "atanisaliti"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This applies to the whole chapter.

source.text: Καὶ ὄντος αὐτοῦ ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ κατακειμένου αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν γυνὴ ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου νάρδου πιστικῆς πολυτελοῦς· συντρίψασα τὴν ἀλάβαστρον κατέχεεν αὐτοῦ τῆς κεφαλῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And being him in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, reclining him, came a woman having an alabaster flask of perfumed oil of nard pure, very costly; having broken the alabaster flask she poured [it] on his head.

en.L: And while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reclining [at table], a woman came having an alabaster flask of perfumed oil, pure nard, very costly; breaking the alabaster flask, she poured [it] over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.
en.B: Jesus was in Bethany, at the home of Simon the leper. While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lay at the meal, a woman came with an alabaster flask of pure nard, a perfumed oil of great value. She broke the flask and poured the oil over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.
en.R: Jesus was in the town of Bethany, eating a meal at the home of Simon. Simon had once had a bad skin disease. A woman came in with a jar made of fine white stone. It was full of very costly perfume made from nard. She broke the jar open and poured the perfume on Jesus' head.

es.L: Y estando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en Betania, en la casa de Simón el leproso, mientras estaba reclinado [a la mesa], vino una mujer que tenía un frasco de alabastro de perfume de nardo puro, muy costoso; quebrando el frasco de alabastro, [se lo] derramó sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cabeza.
es.B: Jesús estaba en Betania, en casa de Simón el leproso. Mientras estaba recostado a la mesa, llegó una mujer con un frasco de alabastro lleno de nardo puro, un perfume de gran valor. Rompió el frasco y derramó el perfume sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cabeza.
es.R: Jesús estaba en el pueblo de Betania, comiendo en casa de Simón. Simón había tenido antes una grave enfermedad de la piel. Llegó una mujer con un frasco hecho de una piedra blanca y fina. Estaba lleno de un perfume de nardo muy caro. Ella rompió el frasco y derramó el perfume sobre la cabeza de Jesús.

sw.L: Na alipokuwa Bethania katika nyumba ya Simoni mkoma, akiwa ameegemea [mezani], alikuja mwanamke mwenye chupa ya alabasta ya manukato ya nardo safi, ya thamani kubwa; akiivunja chupa ya alabasta, akayamimina juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.
sw.B: Yesu alikuwa Bethania, nyumbani kwa Simoni mkoma. Alipokuwa ameegemea mezani akila, mwanamke mmoja alikuja na chupa ya alabasta yenye manukato ya nardo safi, ya thamani kubwa sana. Akaivunja chupa hiyo, akayamimina manukato juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa katika mji wa Bethania, akila chakula nyumbani kwa Simoni. Simoni alikuwa amewahi kuwa na ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi. Mwanamke mmoja aliingia akiwa na chupa iliyotengenezwa kwa jiwe jeupe zuri. Ilikuwa imejaa manukato ya nardo ya bei ghali sana. Akaivunja chupa hiyo, akayamimina manukato hayo juu ya kichwa cha Yesu.

decisions.choice: reclining: lying on a couch at a meal
decisions.reason: At a formal meal guests lay on their left side around a low table, with their feet away from it.

decisions.choice: alabaster flask of pure nard: a sealed stone flask of costly perfumed oil
decisions.reason: Alabaster was a soft white stone used for flasks of perfume. Nard was an oil made from a plant that grows in the Himalayas, so it was rare and very costly. The flask was often sealed, so it was broken at the neck to pour out the oil.

decisions.choice: pure: genuine, not mixed with cheaper oils
decisions.reason: The word is rare and its meaning is not certain. The most likely sense is "genuine" or "pure", from a word for trust.

decisions.choice: poured over his head: an anointing like that of a king
decisions.reason: Kings were anointed on the head (1 Samuel 10:1; 2 Kings 9:6). Jesus himself gives the act another meaning in 14:8: it prepares his body for burial.

decisions.choice: the leper (B); had once had a bad skin disease (R)
alternatives: a man with a serious skin disease
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the name by which Simon was known. Readable says what it meant, as in 1:40, and says "had once had" because he was clearly no longer shut out from others. That is an inference.

decisions.choice: a jar made of fine white stone
decisions.reason: Readable explains what alabaster is.

decisions.choice: reclinado [a la mesa] (L); recostado a la mesa (B)
decisions.reason: Guests at a festive meal lay on couches around a low table (meaning decision m1). "Recostado" keeps that picture; "sentado" would put Jesus on a chair. The same in 14:18.

decisions.choice: ameegemea [mezani] (L); ameegemea mezani (B)
decisions.reason: Guests at a festive meal lay on couches around a low table (meaning decision m1). "Kuegemea" keeps that picture; "kuketi" would put Jesus on a chair. The same in 14:18.

source.text: ἦσαν δέ τινες ἀγανακτοῦντες πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη τοῦ μύρου γέγονεν;

records.literal_gloss: Were now some being indignant among themselves: For what this waste of the perfumed oil has happened?

en.L: Now there were some who were indignant among themselves, "Why has this waste of the perfumed oil happened?
en.B: Some of those present were angry and said to one another, "What is the point of wasting this perfume?
en.R: Some of the people there became angry. They said to each other, "Why did she waste that perfume?

es.L: Y había algunos indignados entre sí: «¿Para qué se ha hecho este desperdicio del perfume?
es.B: Algunos de los presentes se enojaron y se decían unos a otros: «¿Qué sentido tiene desperdiciar este perfume?
es.R: Algunos de los que estaban allí se enojaron. Se decían unos a otros: «¿Por qué desperdició ella ese perfume?

sw.L: Na walikuwapo baadhi waliokasirika miongoni mwao wenyewe, "Upotevu huu wa manukato umetokea kwa nini?
sw.B: Baadhi ya watu waliokuwepo walikasirika, wakaambiana, "Kwa nini manukato haya yapotezwe hivi?
sw.R: Baadhi ya watu waliokuwa pale walikasirika. Wakaambiana, "Kwa nini amepoteza manukato hayo?

decisions.choice: some: some of those at the meal
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who they were. Matthew 26:8 says the disciples, and John 12:4 names Judas.

decisions.choice: among themselves: to one another, or within themselves
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean they spoke among themselves or felt it inwardly. Since their words are given and they rebuke her in 14:5, they seem to have said it to one another.

decisions.choice: waste: loss, something thrown away
decisions.reason: The word means ruin or loss. To them the oil was simply lost.

source.text: ἠδύνατο γὰρ τοῦτο τὸ μύρον πραθῆναι ἐπάνω δηναρίων τριακοσίων καὶ δοθῆναι τοῖς πτωχοῖς· καὶ ἐνεβριμῶντο αὐτῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Could for this the perfumed oil have been sold for more than denarii three hundred and have been given to the poor. And they were scolding her.

en.L: For this perfumed oil could have been sold for more than 300 denarii and given to the poor." And they were scolding her.
en.B: It could have fetched more than {{units:a year's wages|300 denarii}}, and the money could have gone to the poor." So they turned on her with harsh words.
en.R: It could have been sold for more than {{units:a year's pay|300 denarii}}. Then the money could have been given to poor people." And they spoke angrily to her.

es.L: Porque este perfume podía haberse vendido por más de trescientos denarios y [haberse] dado a los pobres». Y la reprendían con dureza.
es.B: Se podría haber vendido por más de {{units:el salario de un año|trescientos denarios}}, y el dinero se habría dado a los pobres». Y la increpaban con palabras duras.
es.R: Se podría haber vendido por más de {{units:lo que gana un trabajador en un año|trescientos denarios}}. Así se habría podido dar el dinero a los pobres». Y le hablaron a ella con enojo.

sw.L: Kwa maana manukato haya yangeweza kuuzwa kwa zaidi ya dinari mia tatu na [fedha] kupewa maskini." Nao walikuwa wakimkemea.
sw.B: Yangeweza kuuzwa kwa zaidi ya {{units:mshahara wa mwaka mzima|dinari mia tatu}}, na fedha hizo zingepewa maskini." Wakamkaripia vikali.
sw.R: Yangeweza kuuzwa kwa zaidi ya {{units:mshahara wa mfanyakazi wa mwaka mzima|dinari mia tatu}}. Kisha fedha hizo zingeweza kupewa maskini." Wakamsemesha kwa hasira.

decisions.choice: 300 denarii: about a year's pay for a worker
decisions.reason: A denarius was a day's wage for a laborer (Matthew 20:2). Three hundred denarii was close to what a worker earned in a year, leaving out Sabbaths and feast days.

decisions.choice: given to the poor: gifts to the poor were expected at Passover
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a duty of the law (Deuteronomy 15:11), and it was the custom to give to them at Passover.

decisions.choice: scolding: speaking sternly, with anger
decisions.reason: The verb is the strong one used in 1:43. It means to speak to someone harshly.

decisions.choice: a year's wages (B); a year's pay (R); 300 denarii as the original unit
decisions.reason: The units setting gives a modern sense of the sum by default and the coin as the alternative. Literal keeps the coin.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἄφετε αὐτήν· τί αὐτῇ κόπους παρέχετε;

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus said, Leave her alone; why to her troubles are you causing?

en.L: But Jesus said, "Leave her alone. Why are you causing her trouble?
en.B: But Jesus said, "Let her be. Why are you bothering her?
en.R: But Jesus said, "Stop bothering her. Why are you giving her a hard time?

es.L: Pero Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Déjenla|Dejadla}}; ¿por qué le {{plural_you:causan|causáis}} molestias?
es.B: Pero Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Déjenla|Dejadla}} en paz. ¿Por qué la {{plural_you:molestan|molestáis}}?
es.R: Pero Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} de molestarla. ¿Por qué le {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} pasar un mal rato?

sw.L: Lakini Yesu alisema, "Mwacheni; kwa nini mnamtaabisha?
sw.B: Lakini Yesu alisema, "Mwacheni. Kwa nini mnamsumbua?
sw.R: Lakini Yesu alisema, "Acheni kumsumbua. Kwa nini mnamletea taabu?

decisions.choice: causing her troubles: making things hard for her
decisions.reason: The phrase means to bother or harass someone.

decisions.choice: leave her alone: stop what you are doing to her
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "forgive", but here it means to let her be.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural "you" (Déjenla|Dejadla, molestan|molestáis)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the chapter.

source.text: καλὸν ἔργον ἠργάσατο ἐν ἐμοί·

records.literal_gloss: A good work she did to me.

en.L: She has done a good work for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: She has done a beautiful thing for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: What she did for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} was very good.

es.L: Una buena obra ha hecho conmigo.
es.B: Ha hecho algo hermoso por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Lo que hizo por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} es muy bueno.

sw.L: Amenitendea kazi njema.
sw.B: Amenitendea jambo zuri sana.
sw.R: Alichonifanyia ni kizuri sana.

decisions.choice: a good work: a fine, fitting deed
decisions.reason: The adjective means good and also fine or beautiful. Jewish teaching counted burying the dead among good works, beyond giving to the poor, and 14:8 links her act to burial.

decisions.choice: beautiful
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the sense of something fine and fitting, not only right.

source.text: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν, καὶ ὅταν θέλητε δύνασθε αὐτοῖς εὖ ποιῆσαι, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε·

records.literal_gloss: Always for the poor you have with yourselves, and whenever you want you are able to them well to do, me but not always you have.

en.L: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want you can do good to them, but you do not always have {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: The poor will be with you at all times, and you can help them any time you wish. But you will not always have {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: There will always be poor people near you. You can help them whenever you want to. But I will not always be here with you.

es.L: Porque siempre {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} a los pobres con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y cuando {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}} {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} hacerles bien, pero a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no siempre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}.
es.B: A los pobres siempre los {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} ayudarlos cuando {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}}. Pero a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no siempre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}}.
es.R: Siempre habrá pobres cerca de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} ayudarlos cuando {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}}. Pero yo no voy a estar siempre aquí con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana maskini mnao pamoja nanyi siku zote, na wakati wowote mtakapo mnaweza kuwatendea mema, lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hamnami siku zote.
sw.B: Maskini mtakuwa nao siku zote, na mnaweza kuwasaidia wakati wowote mnapotaka. Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hamtakuwa {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} siku zote.
sw.R: Siku zote kutakuwa na maskini karibu nanyi. Mnaweza kuwasaidia wakati wowote mnapotaka. Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} sitakuwa hapa pamoja nanyi siku zote.

decisions.choice: you always have the poor with you: an echo of Deuteronomy 15:11
alternatives: a saying that the poor do not matter
decisions.reason: The law says the poor will never cease from the land, and so Israel must open its hand to them. Jesus does not set aside that duty. He says there will be time for it.

decisions.choice: you will not always have me: Jesus speaks of his coming death
alternatives: he is going on a journey
decisions.reason: The words point ahead to 14:8 and to his death within days.

decisions.choice: I will not always be here with you
alternatives: you do not always have me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the words mean in plain terms.

source.text: ὃ ἔσχεν ἐποίησεν, προέλαβεν μυρίσαι τὸ σῶμά μου εἰς τὸν ἐνταφιασμόν.

records.literal_gloss: What she had she did; she took beforehand to anoint my body for the burial.

en.L: She has done what she could; she has anointed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body beforehand for burial.
en.B: She did what was in her power. She has poured perfume on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body ahead of time, to make it ready for burial.
en.R: She did what she was able to do. She put perfume on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body to get it ready to be buried. She did it before the time came.

es.L: Lo que tenía, [lo] hizo; se anticipó a ungir {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo para la sepultura.
es.B: Hizo lo que estaba en su mano: ha perfumado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo de antemano para prepararlo para la sepultura.
es.R: Ella hizo lo que pudo. Puso perfume sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo para prepararlo para el entierro. Lo hizo antes de que llegara el momento.

sw.L: Alichokuwa nacho amekifanya; ametangulia kuupaka mwili {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manukato kwa ajili ya maziko.
sw.B: Amefanya kile alichoweza. Ameupaka mwili {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manukato mapema, ili kuuandaa kwa maziko.
sw.R: Amefanya kile alichoweza kufanya. Ameupaka mwili {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manukato ili kuuandaa kuzikwa. Amefanya hivyo kabla wakati haujafika.

decisions.choice: what she had she did: she did what she could
decisions.reason: The phrase means she did all that lay in her power.

decisions.choice: she took beforehand to anoint: she anointed ahead of time
decisions.reason: The verb "take beforehand" with another verb means to do something in advance.

decisions.choice: for burial: the anointing looks ahead to Jesus' death
alternatives: she knew he was about to die
decisions.reason: Bodies were anointed for burial. In 16:1 the women come to anoint his body and find the tomb empty, so this is the only anointing his body receives. Mark does not say whether she understood this.

source.text: ἀμὴν δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον εἰς ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη λαληθήσεται εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Truly now I say to you, wherever is proclaimed the gospel in the whole world, also what did this [woman] will be spoken for a memorial of her.

en.L: And truly I say to you, wherever the gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her."
en.B: Truly I tell you, in every place in the whole world where the gospel is proclaimed, people will tell what she has done, and remember her."
en.R: I tell you the truth: The good news will be preached in the whole world. And everywhere it is preached, people will tell what this woman did, and they will remember her."

es.L: Y en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: dondequiera que se proclame el evangelio en todo el mundo, también lo que ella ha hecho se contará en memoria de ella».
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que en cualquier lugar del mundo entero donde se anuncie el evangelio, se contará lo que ella ha hecho, y será recordada».
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: la buena noticia se va a anunciar en todo el mundo. Y en todas partes donde se anuncie, la gente contará lo que hizo esta mujer y se acordará de ella».

sw.L: Na kweli nawaambia, popote Injili itakapohubiriwa katika ulimwengu wote, kile alichofanya huyu nacho kitasimuliwa kwa ukumbusho wake."
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, mahali popote katika ulimwengu wote ambapo Injili itahubiriwa, watu watasimulia kile alichofanya mwanamke huyu, naye atakumbukwa."
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: Habari njema itahubiriwa katika ulimwengu wote. Na kila mahali itakapohubiriwa, watu watasimulia kile mwanamke huyu alichofanya, nao watamkumbuka."

decisions.choice: the gospel: the good news about Jesus
alternatives: one of the four written Gospels
decisions.reason: As in 1:1 and 13:10, the word means the message about Jesus, not a book.

decisions.choice: will be spoken: will be told
decisions.reason: The passive leaves open who tells it; those who proclaim the gospel will tell her story with it.

decisions.choice: for a memorial of her: so that she is remembered
alternatives: a memorial before God, like an offering
decisions.reason: The word can mean an offering that reminds God (Acts 10:4), but here it means that people will remember her.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The same forms as elsewhere in Mark.

decisions.choice: En verdad les|os digo (L, B); Les|Os digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus's solemn opening, used throughout Mark and recorded once in this chapter. "De cierto" is the older church wording; Readable says it in plain words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: el evangelio (L, B); la buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: The good news about Jesus (meaning decision m1). Balanced keeps the usual name of the message; Readable says what the word means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus's solemn opening, used throughout Mark and recorded once in this chapter. Readable puts it in plain words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Injili (L, B); habari njema (R)
decisions.reason: The good news about Jesus (meaning decision m1). Balanced keeps the usual name of the message; Readable says what the word means, as the English does.

source.text: Καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριὼθ ὁ εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδοῖ αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And Judas Iscariot, the one of the Twelve, went away to the chief priests so that him he might hand over to them.

en.L: And Judas Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve, went away to the chief priests in order to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to them.
en.B: Then one of the Twelve, Judas Iscariot, went off to the chief priests to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to them.
en.R: Then Judas Iscariot went to the leading priests. He was one of Jesus' twelve followers. He went to offer to help them arrest Jesus.

es.L: Y Judas Iscariote, el uno de los Doce, se fue a los jefes de los sacerdotes para entregárselo.
es.B: Entonces uno de los Doce, Judas Iscariote, fue a ver a los jefes de los sacerdotes para traicionarlo y entregárselo.
es.R: Entonces Judas Iscariote fue a ver a los jefes de los sacerdotes. Era uno de los doce discípulos de Jesús. Fue a ofrecerles su ayuda para arrestar a Jesús.

sw.L: Na Yuda Iskariote, yule mmoja wa wale Kumi na Wawili, alikwenda kwa wakuu wa makuhani ili amkabidhi kwao.
sw.B: Kisha Yuda Iskariote, mmoja wa wale Kumi na Wawili, alikwenda kwa wakuu wa makuhani ili amsaliti kwao.
sw.R: Kisha Yuda Iskariote alikwenda kwa wakuu wa makuhani. Yeye alikuwa mmoja wa wanafunzi kumi na wawili wa Yesu. Alikwenda kujitolea kuwasaidia kumkamata Yesu.

decisions.choice: hand over: give Jesus up to his enemies, a betrayal by a friend
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over, and it is the word Jesus used of his own coming death (9:31; 10:33). When Judas is the subject, it means betrayal.

decisions.choice: the one of the Twelve: one of the Twelve, as everyone knew
decisions.reason: The article may point to him as the one already known from 3:19. Mark stresses that the betrayer was one of Jesus' closest followers.

decisions.choice: hand over (L); betray (B); help them arrest (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word that links this to Jesus' sayings about being handed over. Balanced and Readable name the betrayal.

decisions.choice: entregar (L); traicionar y entregar (B); ayudar a arrestar (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is "hand over", here a betrayal by a friend (meaning decision m1). Balanced keeps both the betrayal and the handing over, since Spanish "traicionar" alone does not say he gave Jesus up to them. Readable says "discípulos" for the English "followers", as throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: kumkabidhi (L); kumsaliti (B); kuwasaidia kumkamata (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is "hand over", here a betrayal by a friend (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the plain "kukabidhi" (hand over) and Balanced says "kusaliti" (betray), as the English does, through the chapter. Readable says "wanafunzi" for the English "followers", as throughout Mark.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐχάρησαν καὶ ἐπηγγείλαντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard they rejoiced and promised him silver to give.

en.L: And when they heard [it], they rejoiced and promised to give him money.
en.B: They were delighted to hear it and promised to pay him.
en.R: The priests were very happy when they heard this. They promised to give Judas money.

es.L: Y ellos, al oír[lo], se alegraron y prometieron darle dinero.
es.B: Ellos se alegraron mucho al oírlo y prometieron pagarle.
es.R: Los sacerdotes se pusieron muy contentos al oír esto. Prometieron darle dinero a Judas.

sw.L: Nao waliposikia walifurahi, wakaahidi kumpa fedha.
sw.B: Waliposikia hivyo walifurahi sana, wakaahidi kumlipa.
sw.R: Makuhani walifurahi sana waliposikia jambo hilo. Wakaahidi kumpa Yuda fedha.

decisions.choice: silver: money
decisions.reason: The word means silver and was used of money in general. Matthew 26:15 gives the sum as thirty pieces of silver.

decisions.choice: they rejoiced: the leaders' problem of 14:1-2 is solved
decisions.reason: One of Jesus' own followers offers a way to take him quietly.

source.text: καὶ ἐζήτει πῶς αὐτὸν εὐκαίρως παραδοῖ.

records.literal_gloss: And he was seeking how him conveniently he might hand over.

en.L: And he was seeking how he might conveniently hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.
en.B: So Judas looked for a good chance to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: From then on Judas watched for the right time to hand Jesus over to them.

es.L: Y buscaba cómo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregaría en un momento oportuno.
es.B: Así que Judas buscaba una buena ocasión para traicionarlo.
es.R: Desde entonces Judas esperaba el momento oportuno para entregarles a Jesús.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akitafuta jinsi atakavyomkabidhi kwa wakati unaofaa.
sw.B: Basi Yuda akatafuta nafasi nzuri ya kumsaliti.
sw.R: Tangu wakati huo Yuda alikuwa akivizia wakati unaofaa wa kumtia Yesu mikononi mwao.

decisions.choice: conveniently: at a good moment, when no crowd was near
decisions.reason: The leaders wanted to avoid the crowds (14:2), so Judas looked for a time when Jesus was away from them.

decisions.choice: betray (B); hand ... over to them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced names the betrayal as in 14:10. Readable spells out to whom he was handed over.

source.text: Καὶ τῇ πρώτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν ἀζύμων, ὅτε τὸ πάσχα ἔθυον, λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ· Ποῦ θέλεις ἀπελθόντες ἑτοιμάσωμεν ἵνα φάγῃς τὸ πάσχα;

records.literal_gloss: And on the first day of the Unleavened [Bread], when the Passover they were sacrificing, say to him the disciples of him, Where do you want having gone we should prepare so that you may eat the Passover?

en.L: And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they were sacrificing the Passover [lamb], {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to go and prepare for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to eat the Passover?"
en.B: On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the day the Passover lambs were sacrificed, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where would {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} like us to go and make ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to eat the Passover meal?"
en.R: It was the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread. On this day the lambs were killed for the Passover meal. Jesus' followers said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where should we go to make the Passover meal ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

es.L: Y el primer día de los Panes sin Levadura, cuando sacrificaban [el cordero de] la Pascua, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿Dónde quieres que vayamos a preparar para que comas la Pascua?».
es.B: El primer día de los Panes sin Levadura, cuando se sacrificaban los corderos de la Pascua, {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¿Dónde quieres que vayamos a prepararte la cena de Pascua?».
es.R: Era el primer día de la fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura. Ese día se mataban los corderos para la cena de la Pascua. Los discípulos de Jesús {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Dónde quieres que vayamos a preparar la cena de la Pascua para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?».

sw.L: Na siku ya kwanza ya Mikate Isiyo na Chachu, walipokuwa wakichinja [mwanakondoo wa] Pasaka, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wanamwambia, "Unataka twende tukuandalie wapi uile Pasaka?"
sw.B: Siku ya kwanza ya Mikate Isiyo na Chachu, siku ambayo wanakondoo wa Pasaka walichinjwa, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimwuliza, "Unataka twende wapi tukuandalie chakula cha Pasaka?"
sw.R: Ilikuwa siku ya kwanza ya Sikukuu ya Mikate Isiyo na Chachu. Siku hiyo wanakondoo walichinjwa kwa ajili ya chakula cha Pasaka. Wanafunzi wa Yesu walimwuliza, "Tuende wapi tukakuandalie chakula cha Pasaka?"

decisions.choice: say: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, past events are told in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: they asked. Mark does the same many times in this chapter.

decisions.choice: the first day ... when they sacrificed the Passover: 14 Nisan
alternatives: 15 Nisan, the day after the meal
decisions.reason: The lambs were killed in the temple on the afternoon of 14 Nisan and eaten that evening, when 15 Nisan began. People also spoke of 14 Nisan as the first day of the festival, because all yeast was removed from houses that day.

decisions.choice: the Passover: the Passover meal, with its lamb
decisions.reason: Here the word means the meal, as "eat the Passover" shows.

decisions.choice: the Passover meal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the meal is meant.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dicen); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (dijeron, preguntaron)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of this chapter in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanamwambia); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of this chapter in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same throughout the chapter.

source.text: καὶ ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ ἀπαντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων· ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ, καὶ ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθῃ εἴπατε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅτι Ὁ διδάσκαλος λέγει· Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμά μου ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;

records.literal_gloss: And he sends two of the disciples of him and says to them, Go into the city, and will meet you a man a jar of water carrying; follow him, \v 14 and wherever he enters say to the master of the house that The Teacher says, Where is the guest room of me where the Passover with the disciples of me I may eat?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and says to them, "Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him, \v 14 and wherever he goes in, say to the owner of the house, 'The Teacher says, "Where is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} guest room where I may eat the Passover with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples?"'
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent off two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples with these instructions: "Go into the city. A man carrying a water jar will come to meet you. Follow him, \v 14 and when he goes into a house, tell the owner of the house, 'The Teacher says, "Which is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} guest room, where I am to eat the Passover with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples?"'
en.R: Jesus sent two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers into Jerusalem. He told them, "Go into the city. You will meet a man who is carrying a jar of water. Follow him. \v 14 He will go into a house. Say to the owner of that house, 'The Teacher wants to know, "Where is the room for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to stay in? I want to eat the Passover meal there with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers."'

es.L: Y envía a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y les dice: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la ciudad, y {{plural_you:les|os}} saldrá al encuentro un hombre que lleva un cántaro de agua; {{plural_you:síganlo|seguidlo}}, \v 14 y dondequiera que entre, {{plural_you:digan|decid}} al dueño de la casa: “El Maestro dice: ‘¿Dónde está {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} aposento, donde pueda comer la Pascua con {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} discípulos?’”.
es.B: Entonces envió a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos con estas instrucciones: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la ciudad. Un hombre que lleva un cántaro de agua {{plural_you:les|os}} saldrá al encuentro. {{plural_you:Síganlo|Seguidlo}}, \v 14 y cuando entre en una casa, {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}} al dueño: “El Maestro pregunta: ‘¿Cuál es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} habitación, donde voy a comer la Pascua con {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} discípulos?’”.
es.R: Jesús envió a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos a Jerusalén. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la ciudad. Allí {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} a un hombre que lleva un cántaro de agua. {{plural_you:Síganlo|Seguidlo}}. \v 14 Él va a entrar en una casa. {{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}} al dueño de esa casa: “El Maestro quiere saber: ‘¿Dónde está la habitación para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}? Quiero comer allí la cena de la Pascua con {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} discípulos’”.

sw.L: Naye anawatuma wawili wa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na kuwaambia, "Nendeni mjini, na mtu anayebeba mtungi wa maji atakutana nanyi; mfuateni, \v 14 na popote atakapoingia, mwambieni mwenye nyumba, 'Mwalimu anasema, "Kiko wapi chumba {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} cha wageni, ambamo nitaila Pasaka pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}?"'
sw.B: Basi aliwatuma wawili wa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akawaambia, "Nendeni mjini. Mtu mmoja anayebeba mtungi wa maji atakutana nanyi. Mfuateni, \v 14 na atakapoingia katika nyumba, mwambieni mwenye nyumba hiyo, 'Mwalimu anauliza, "Kiko wapi chumba {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} cha wageni, ambamo nitakula Pasaka pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}?"'
sw.R: Yesu aliwatuma wawili wa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwenda Yerusalemu. Akawaambia, "Nendeni mjini. Mtakutana na mtu anayebeba mtungi wa maji. Mfuateni. \v 14 Ataingia katika nyumba fulani. Mwambieni mwenye nyumba hiyo, 'Mwalimu anataka kujua, "Kiko wapi chumba cha kukaa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}? Nataka kula chakula cha Pasaka humo pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."'

decisions.choice: a man carrying a jar of water: an unusual sight that would stand out
decisions.reason: Women usually carried water in jars; men carried it in skins. A man with a jar would be easy to pick out.

decisions.choice: Jesus' knowledge of what will happen
alternatives: only a plan made in advance with the owner
decisions.reason: Mark tells this as in 11:2-6: things happen as Jesus says. Whether Jesus had arranged it beforehand or foresaw it, Mark does not say.

decisions.choice: guest room: a room where guests lodge or eat
decisions.reason: The word is the one used at Luke 2:7. It means a lodging or guest room in a house.

decisions.choice: the Teacher: Jesus, as his followers called him
alternatives: a title the owner gave him
decisions.reason: The owner seems to know who "the Teacher" is, which suggests he was a follower or friend.

decisions.choice: into Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city.

decisions.choice: aposento (L); habitación (B, R)
decisions.reason: A room where guests could lodge or eat (meaning decision m3). "Aposento" is the older word for a room in a house; Balanced and Readable use the everyday "habitación". "Mesón" is an inn, which this was not.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on Jesus's own possessives (changu, wangu) and on mimi
alternatives: no span where the English has none
decisions.reason: When Jesus speaks of himself the English marks "my" and "me" but not "I". Swahili spans the free possessives and "mimi", as its style guide says, so the Swahili spans fall on slightly different words from the English. This holds for the whole chapter.

source.text: καὶ αὐτὸς ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον ἕτοιμον· καὶ ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε ἡμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And he you will show an upper room large, furnished, ready; and there prepare for us.

en.L: And he himself will show you a large upper room, furnished [and] ready; and prepare [it] for us there."
en.B: He himself will show you a big upper room, set out with couches and ready. Get things ready for us there."
en.R: He will show you a large room upstairs. It will have everything you need. Get the meal ready for us there."

es.L: Y él mismo {{plural_you:les|os}} mostrará un aposento alto, grande, dispuesto [y] listo; y allí {{plural_you:preparen|preparad}} para nosotros».
es.B: Él mismo {{plural_you:les|os}} mostrará en el piso de arriba una sala grande, con los divanes dispuestos y lista. {{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} allí lo necesario para nosotros».
es.R: Él {{plural_you:les|os}} mostrará una sala grande en el piso de arriba. Tendrá todo lo que {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}}. {{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} allí la cena para nosotros».

sw.L: Naye mwenyewe atawaonyesha chumba kikubwa cha ghorofani, kilichotandikwa, kilicho tayari; na huko mtuandalie."
sw.B: Yeye mwenyewe atawaonyesha chumba kikubwa cha ghorofani, kilichotandikwa viti vya kuegemea na kilicho tayari. Tuandalieni humo."
sw.R: Atawaonyesha chumba kikubwa ghorofani. Kitakuwa na kila kitu mnachohitaji. Tuandalieni chakula humo."

decisions.choice: furnished: spread with couches and cushions for a meal
decisions.reason: The word means spread or laid out. In a dining room it means the couches were in place for reclining at the meal.

decisions.choice: he himself: the owner of the house
decisions.reason: The pronoun is emphatic and points back to the owner of 14:14.

decisions.choice: set out with couches
decisions.reason: Balanced says what furnishing a dining room meant.

source.text: καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εὗρον καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.

records.literal_gloss: And went out the disciples and came into the city and found as he said to them, and they prepared the Passover.

en.L: And the disciples went out and came into the city and found [it] just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
en.B: So the disciples set out, came into the city and found it all as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said, and there they prepared the Passover.
en.R: The two followers went into the city. Everything happened just as Jesus had told them. So they got the Passover meal ready there.

es.L: Y salieron los discípulos y fueron a la ciudad y encontraron [todo] tal como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les había dicho, y prepararon la Pascua.
es.B: Los discípulos salieron, llegaron a la ciudad y encontraron todo tal como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les había dicho; y allí prepararon la Pascua.
es.R: Los dos discípulos fueron a la ciudad. Todo pasó tal como Jesús les había dicho. Así que prepararon allí la cena de la Pascua.

sw.L: Na wanafunzi walitoka, wakaenda mjini, wakakuta [kila kitu] kama alivyowaambia, wakaiandaa Pasaka.
sw.B: Wanafunzi waliondoka, wakafika mjini, wakakuta kila kitu kama alivyokuwa amewaambia. Wakaiandaa Pasaka huko.
sw.R: Wale wanafunzi wawili walikwenda mjini. Kila kitu kilitokea kama Yesu alivyokuwa amewaambia. Basi wakaandaa chakula cha Pasaka huko.

decisions.choice: prepared the Passover: had the lamb killed at the temple and readied the meal
decisions.reason: Getting the meal ready meant taking the lamb to the temple to be sacrificed, roasting it, and setting out unleavened bread, bitter herbs and wine.

decisions.choice: the two followers
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the two sent in 14:13 are meant.

source.text: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἔρχεται μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα.

records.literal_gloss: And evening having come he comes with the Twelve.

en.L: And when evening came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes with the Twelve.
en.B: When evening came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} arrived with the Twelve.
en.R: That evening Jesus came to the house with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve followers.

es.L: Y llegada la tarde, viene con los Doce.
es.B: Al caer la tarde, llegó con los Doce.
es.R: Esa noche, Jesús llegó a la casa con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce discípulos.

sw.L: Na ilipokuwa jioni, anakuja pamoja na wale Kumi na Wawili.
sw.B: Ilipofika jioni, alikuja pamoja na wale Kumi na Wawili.
sw.R: Jioni ile Yesu alifika kwenye nyumba ile pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili.

decisions.choice: evening: the Passover meal was eaten at night
decisions.reason: The law says the lamb is eaten that night (Exodus 12:8). With sunset 15 Nisan began.

decisions.choice: came to the house with his twelve followers
decisions.reason: Readable says where he came and who the Twelve were.

source.text: καὶ ἀνακειμένων αὐτῶν καὶ ἐσθιόντων ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν παραδώσει με ὁ ἐσθίων μετ’ ἐμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And reclining them and eating, Jesus said, Truly I say to you that one of you will hand over me, the [one] eating with me.

en.L: And as they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, "Truly I say to you that one of you will hand {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over, the one who is eating with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: As they lay at the table and ate, Jesus told them, "Truly I tell you, one of you here, eating with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, will betray {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: While they were eating, Jesus said, "I tell you the truth: one of you will betray {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. He is eating here with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} now."

es.L: Y estando ellos reclinados y comiendo, Jesús dijo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} entregará, el que come conmigo».
es.B: Mientras estaban recostados a la mesa comiendo, Jesús les dijo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, uno que come conmigo, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} va a traicionar».
es.R: Mientras comían, Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} va a traicionar. Está comiendo aquí conmigo ahora».

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wameegemea mezani na kula, Yesu alisema, "Kweli nawaambia kwamba mmoja wenu atanikabidhi, yeye anayekula pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}."
sw.B: Walipokuwa wameegemea mezani wakila, Yesu aliwaambia, "Kweli nawaambia, mmoja wenu, anayekula pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}, atanisaliti."
sw.R: Walipokuwa wakila, Yesu alisema, "Nawaambia ukweli: mmoja wenu atanisaliti. Anakula hapa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} sasa hivi."

decisions.choice: the one eating with me: an echo of Psalm 41:10
alternatives: only a description of where he sat
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks of a close friend "who ate my bread" lifting his heel against the psalmist. To betray someone you had eaten with was a deep wrong.

decisions.choice: hand over: betray
decisions.reason: As in 14:10, the verb used of Judas means betrayal.

decisions.choice: hand over (L); betray (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same choice as in 14:10.

source.text: ἤρξαντο λυπεῖσθαι καὶ λέγειν αὐτῷ εἷς κατὰ εἷς· Μήτι ἐγώ;

records.literal_gloss: They began to be grieved and to say to him one by one, Surely not I?

en.L: They began to be grieved and to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} one by one, "Surely not I?"
en.B: They were deeply hurt, and one after another they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "It is not I, is it?"
en.R: The followers became very sad. One after another, they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You do not mean me, do you?"

es.L: Comenzaron a entristecerse y a decirle uno por uno: «¿Acaso yo?».
es.B: Ellos se pusieron muy tristes y, uno tras otro, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} decían: «No seré yo, ¿verdad?».
es.R: Los discípulos se pusieron muy tristes. Uno tras otro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaban: «No te refieres a mí, ¿verdad?».

sw.L: Walianza kuhuzunika na kumwambia mmoja mmoja, "Hakika si mimi?"
sw.B: Wakahuzunika sana, na mmoja baada ya mwingine wakaanza kumwuliza, "Si mimi, sivyo?"
sw.R: Wanafunzi walihuzunika sana. Mmoja baada ya mwingine wakamwuliza, "Humaanishi mimi, sivyo?"

decisions.choice: surely not I?: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question is put in a form that hopes for "no". Each one wants to be told it is not he.

decisions.choice: Surely not I?, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Surely not I? And another, Surely not I?
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and another said, Surely not I?". The earliest manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: You do not mean me, do you?
decisions.reason: Readable puts the question in everyday words that keep its hopeful tone.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Εἷς τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ ἐμβαπτόμενος μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὸ τρύβλιον·

records.literal_gloss: But he said to them, One of the Twelve, the [one] dipping with me into the bowl.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "[It is] one of the Twelve, the one who is dipping with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} into the bowl.
en.B: He said to them, "It is one of the Twelve, one who dips bread into the bowl with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Jesus answered, "It is one of you twelve. He is dipping his bread into the same bowl as I am.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «[Es] uno de los Doce, el que moja conmigo en el plato.
es.B: Él les dijo: «Es uno de los Doce, uno que moja el pan en el plato conmigo.
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Es uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} doce. Está mojando su pan en el mismo plato que yo.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "[Ni] mmoja wa wale Kumi na Wawili, yule anayechovya pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} katika bakuli.
sw.B: Akawaambia, "Ni mmoja wa wale Kumi na Wawili, anayechovya mkate katika bakuli pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Ni mmoja wenu ninyi kumi na wawili. Anachovya mkate wake katika bakuli lile lile ninalochovya {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.

decisions.choice: dipping into the bowl: sharing the same dish of sauce at the meal
alternatives: a sign that points out one man
decisions.reason: At the Passover meal bread and herbs were dipped into a shared bowl of sauce. Jesus does not name the man; the words stress that the betrayer is a close companion.

decisions.choice: dipping: now, at this meal
decisions.reason: The present participle describes one who shares the meal now, not one who will dip next.

decisions.choice: his bread
decisions.reason: Readable says what was dipped.

source.text: ὅτι ὁ μὲν υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑπάγει καθὼς γέγραπται περὶ αὐτοῦ, οὐαὶ δὲ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ δι’ οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται· καλὸν αὐτῷ εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος.

records.literal_gloss: For indeed the Son of Man goes as it has been written concerning him, woe but to the man that through whom the Son of Man is handed over; good for him if not had been born the man that.

en.L: For the Son of Man goes just as it has been written about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! [It would be] good for him if that man had not been born."
en.B: The Son of Man is going as it stands written about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but how terrible for the man who betrays the Son of Man! It would be good for that man if he had never been born."
en.R: The Son of Man will die, just as the Scriptures say. But how terrible it will be for the man who betrays {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! That man would be better off never being born."

es.L: Porque el Hijo del Hombre se va, tal como está escrito acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}; pero ¡ay de aquel hombre por medio del cual el Hijo del Hombre es entregado! Bueno [sería] para él si no hubiera nacido aquel hombre».
es.B: El Hijo del Hombre se va, como la Escritura dice de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}; pero ¡ay de aquel hombre que traiciona al Hijo del Hombre! Para ese hombre sería mejor no haber nacido».
es.R: El Hijo del Hombre va a morir, tal como dicen las Escrituras. Pero ¡qué terrible será para el hombre que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} traiciona! Para ese hombre sería mejor no haber nacido nunca».

sw.L: Kwa maana Mwana wa Adamu anaenda kama ilivyoandikwa juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, lakini ole wake mtu yule ambaye kupitia kwake Mwana wa Adamu anakabidhiwa! [Ingekuwa] vema kwake kama mtu yule asingezaliwa."
sw.B: Mwana wa Adamu anaenda kama Maandiko yanavyosema juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, lakini ole wake mtu yule anayemsaliti Mwana wa Adamu! Ingekuwa vema kwa mtu huyo kama asingezaliwa kamwe."
sw.R: Mwana wa Adamu atakufa, kama Maandiko yanavyosema. Lakini itakuwa vibaya sana kwa mtu yule anayemsaliti! Ingekuwa afadhali mtu huyo asingezaliwa kabisa."

decisions.choice: goes: goes to his death
decisions.reason: To "go" is a way of speaking of death. Jesus' death follows the path set out in Scripture.

decisions.choice: as it has been written: the Scriptures about the suffering of God's servant
decisions.reason: Mark does not name a passage. Texts such as Isaiah 53 and Psalm 22 speak of a righteous sufferer (see 9:12).

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and warning
decisions.reason: The word mourns what is coming upon the man and warns of it at the same time.

decisions.choice: God's plan and human guilt together
alternatives: Judas only did what was fated
decisions.reason: The death is foretold in Scripture, but the one who betrays Jesus is still held responsible.

decisions.choice: betrays (B, R)
decisions.reason: Where the one through whom it happens is Judas, Balanced and Readable name the betrayal. Literal keeps "handed over".

decisions.choice: will die, just as the Scriptures say
alternatives: goes as it is written about him
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "goes" means and what is written.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre; está escrito (L), la Escritura dice (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms used throughout Mark, recorded once in this chapter.

decisions.choice: ¡ay de! (L, B); qué terrible será (R)
alternatives: qué terrible at Balanced, as the English
decisions.reason: A cry of grief and warning (meaning decision m3). Spanish "¡ay de...!" still carries both and is the word used for this cry throughout the Gospels; Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu; imeandikwa (L), Maandiko yanasema (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms used throughout Mark, recorded once in this chapter.

decisions.choice: ole wake (L, B); itakuwa vibaya sana (R)
decisions.reason: A cry of grief and warning (meaning decision m3). "Ole" carries both, as the Gospels use it throughout; Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

source.text: Καὶ ἐσθιόντων αὐτῶν λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐλογήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς καὶ εἶπεν· Λάβετε, τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου.

records.literal_gloss: And eating them, having taken bread, having blessed, he broke and gave to them and said, Take; this is the body of me.

en.L: And as they were eating, taking bread [and] blessing [God], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke [it] and gave [it] to them and said, "Take; this is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body."
en.B: During the meal {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took bread, spoke the blessing, broke it and handed it to them, saying, "Take it. This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body."
en.R: While they were eating, Jesus took some bread and thanked God for it. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke it, gave it to them, and said, "Take this. It is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body."

es.L: Y mientras ellos comían, tomando pan [y] bendiciendo [a Dios], [lo] partió y [se lo] dio y dijo: «{{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}}; esto es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo».
es.B: Mientras comían, tomó pan, pronunció la bendición, lo partió y se lo dio, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}}. Esto es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo».
es.R: Mientras comían, Jesús tomó un pan y dio gracias a Dios por él. Luego lo partió, se lo dio a ellos y dijo: «{{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} esto. Es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo».

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wakila, akichukua mkate [na] kusema baraka, aliumega, akawapa, akasema, "Chukueni; huu ni mwili {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakila, alichukua mkate, akasema baraka, akaumega, akawapa, akisema, "Chukueni. Huu ni mwili {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."
sw.R: Walipokuwa wakila, Yesu alichukua mkate, akamshukuru Mungu kwa ajili yake. Kisha akaumega, akawapa, akasema, "Chukueni huu. Ni mwili {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."

decisions.choice: having blessed: having said the blessing over the bread, which praises God
decisions.reason: A Jewish blessing at a meal praised God who brings bread from the earth. The blessing is addressed to God, as the thanks over the cup in 14:23 is.

decisions.choice: this is my body: the bread is given as Jesus himself, given up in death
alternatives: only a picture with no further meaning
decisions.reason: Christians have understood these words in different ways. The text gives the words as Jesus said them, with the link to his death that 14:24 makes plain.

decisions.choice: Take, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts add "eat", as in Matthew 26:26. The earliest manuscripts have "Take" alone. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: thanked God for it
decisions.reason: Readable says what the blessing was.

decisions.choice: kusema baraka
decisions.reason: The blessing said over the bread praises God (meaning decision m1). "Kubariki mkate" would read as blessing the bread itself; "kusema baraka" is saying the blessing, and Readable names the thanks to God, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ λαβὼν ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἔπιον ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken a cup, having given thanks, he gave to them, and they drank from it all.

en.L: And taking a cup [and] giving thanks, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave [it] to them, and they all drank from it.
en.B: He also took a cup, and after giving thanks {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} passed it to them, and every one of them drank from it.
en.R: Then Jesus took a cup of wine. He thanked God for it and gave it to them. All of them drank some of it.

es.L: Y tomando una copa [y] dando gracias, [se la] dio, y bebieron de ella todos.
es.B: Tomó también una copa, y después de dar gracias se la pasó, y todos bebieron de ella.
es.R: Luego Jesús tomó una copa de vino. Dio gracias a Dios y se la dio a ellos. Todos bebieron un poco.

sw.L: Na akichukua kikombe [na] kushukuru, aliwapa, na wote wakanywa kutoka humo.
sw.B: Kisha alichukua kikombe, akashukuru, akawapa, nao wote wakanywa kutoka humo.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alichukua kikombe cha divai. Akamshukuru Mungu, akawapa. Wote wakanywa kidogo.

decisions.choice: a cup: a cup of wine at the Passover meal
decisions.reason: Wine was drunk at the Passover meal. Jewish writings from a little later speak of four cups through the evening. Mark does not say which cup this was.

decisions.choice: giving thanks: thanking God
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used at the feeding of the four thousand (8:6). From it comes the later name Eucharist.

decisions.choice: a cup of wine
decisions.reason: Readable says what was in the cup, as 14:25 shows.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά μου τῆς διαθήκης τὸ ἐκχυννόμενον ὑπὲρ πολλῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, This is the blood of me of the covenant, the [blood] being poured out for many.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.
en.B: He said to them, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood of the covenant, poured out for many.
en.R: Jesus said to them, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood. It puts God's covenant into effect. It is poured out for many people.

es.L: Y les dijo: «Esto es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sangre del pacto, la que es derramada por muchos.
es.B: Les dijo: «Esta es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sangre del pacto, derramada por muchos.
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Esta es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} sangre. Con ella el pacto de Dios entra en vigor. Se derrama por mucha gente.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Hii ni damu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ya agano, ile inayomwagwa kwa ajili ya wengi.
sw.B: Akawaambia, "Hii ni damu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ya agano, inayomwagwa kwa ajili ya wengi.
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Hii ni damu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Inalifanya agano la Mungu lianze kutumika. Inamwagwa kwa ajili ya watu wengi.

decisions.choice: blood of the covenant: Exodus 24:8
alternatives: a new phrase with no background
decisions.reason: At Sinai Moses sprinkled the people with blood and said, "See the blood of the covenant." Jesus' blood seals a covenant as the sacrifice at Sinai did.

decisions.choice: the covenant, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "the new covenant", as in Luke 22:20 and 1 Corinthians 11:25. The earliest manuscripts do not have "new". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: poured out for many: an echo of Isaiah 53:12 and Mark 10:45
decisions.reason: The servant of Isaiah 53 "poured out his life to death" and bore the sin of many. "Many" stresses the great number; it does not mean that some are left out.

decisions.choice: being poured out: a present that looks to what is about to happen
decisions.reason: His blood is about to be shed. The present makes the coming death certain.

decisions.choice: It puts God's covenant into effect
decisions.reason: Readable says what "blood of the covenant" means: blood that makes the covenant binding.

decisions.choice: pacto
decisions.reason: The covenant of Exodus 24:8 (meaning decision m1), "pacto" as in Hebrews and Romans. "Testamento" would read as a will.

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ πίω ἐκ τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ὅταν αὐτὸ πίνω καινὸν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you that no longer not not I will drink of the fruit of the vine until the day that when it I drink new in the kingdom of God.

en.L: Truly I say to you that I will no longer drink at all of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
en.B: Truly I tell you, I will never again drink the fruit of the vine until the day I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
en.R: I tell you the truth: I will not drink wine again until the day when I drink new wine in God's kingdom."

es.L: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ya no beberé nunca más del fruto de la vid hasta aquel día en que lo beba nuevo en el reino de Dios».
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que no volveré a beber del fruto de la vid hasta el día en que lo beba nuevo en el reino de Dios».
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: no volveré a beber vino hasta el día en que beba vino nuevo en el reino de Dios».

sw.L: Kweli nawaambia kwamba sitakunywa tena kamwe tunda la mzabibu mpaka siku ile nitakapolinywa jipya katika ufalme wa Mungu."
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, sitakunywa tena tunda la mzabibu mpaka siku ile nitakapolinywa jipya katika ufalme wa Mungu."
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: Sitakunywa divai tena mpaka siku ile nitakapokunywa divai mpya katika ufalme wa Mungu."

decisions.choice: the fruit of the vine: wine
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from the Jewish blessing over wine.

decisions.choice: no longer ... not at all: a strong denial
decisions.reason: Greek here piles up negatives to make the denial as strong as possible.

decisions.choice: new in the kingdom of God: at the feast when God's rule has fully come
decisions.reason: "New" points to a new kind of life. The prophets pictured God's rule as a great banquet (Isaiah 25:6). Jesus looks beyond his death to that day.

decisions.choice: wine; new wine
alternatives: the fruit of the vine; it new
decisions.reason: Readable names the wine and says plainly what will be new.

source.text: Καὶ ὑμνήσαντες ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And having sung a hymn they went out to the Mount of the Olives.

en.L: And after singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
en.B: Then they sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives.
en.R: Then they sang a song of praise to God and went out to the Mount of Olives.

es.L: Y después de cantar el himno, salieron hacia el monte de los Olivos.
es.B: Luego cantaron un himno y salieron hacia el monte de los Olivos.
es.R: Luego cantaron un canto de alabanza a Dios y salieron hacia el monte de los Olivos.

sw.L: Na walipokwisha kuimba wimbo, walitoka kwenda Mlima wa Mizeituni.
sw.B: Kisha waliimba wimbo, wakaondoka kwenda Mlima wa Mizeituni.
sw.R: Kisha waliimba wimbo wa kumsifu Mungu, wakatoka wakaenda Mlima wa Mizeituni.

decisions.choice: a hymn: the psalms of praise sung at the close of the Passover meal
decisions.reason: Psalms 113-118, called the Hallel, were sung at Passover, the last part at the end of the meal. Mark does not say which song they sang.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the hill east of Jerusalem
alternatives: a hill far from the city
decisions.reason: During the festival pilgrims were to stay within the area of greater Jerusalem, which included this hill across the Kidron valley.

decisions.choice: a song of praise to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word.

source.text: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Πάντες σκανδαλισθήσεσθε, ὅτι γέγραπται· Πατάξω τὸν ποιμένα, καὶ τὰ πρόβατα διασκορπισθήσονται.

records.literal_gloss: And says to them Jesus that All you will fall away, because it has been written, I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.

en.L: And Jesus says to them, "You will all fall away, because it is written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'
en.B: Jesus told them, "All of you will stumble and fall away, for it stands written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'
en.R: Then Jesus told them, "Every one of you will turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. The Scriptures say, 'I will strike down the shepherd, and the sheep will run off in all directions.'

es.L: Y les dice Jesús: «Todos {{plural_you:caerán|caeréis}}, porque está escrito: “Heriré al pastor, y las ovejas serán dispersadas”.
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «Todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:tropezarán|tropezaréis}} y {{plural_you:caerán|caeréis}}, porque la Escritura dice: “Heriré al pastor, y las ovejas se dispersarán”.
es.R: Entonces Jesús les dijo: «Todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:van|vais}} a abandonar. Las Escrituras dicen: “Voy a herir al pastor, y las ovejas se escaparán por todas partes”.

sw.L: Naye Yesu anawaambia, "Nyote mtajikwaa, kwa maana imeandikwa, 'Nitampiga mchungaji, na kondoo watatawanyika.'
sw.B: Yesu aliwaambia, "Ninyi nyote mtajikwaa na kuanguka, kwa maana Maandiko yanasema, 'Nitampiga mchungaji, na kondoo watatawanyika.'
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaambia, "Kila mmoja wenu ataniacha. Maandiko yanasema, 'Nitamwangusha mchungaji, na kondoo watakimbia kila upande.'

decisions.choice: fall away: be tripped up so as to desert him
decisions.reason: The verb means to stumble or be caused to sin. Here it means they will desert Jesus when he is arrested (14:50), not that they will be lost for good, as 14:28 shows.

decisions.choice: I will strike the shepherd: Zechariah 13:7
decisions.reason: In Zechariah God calls for the sword to strike his shepherd so that the sheep scatter. Mark gives it in the first person, "I will strike", which makes plain that God is the one acting.

decisions.choice: I: God himself
decisions.reason: Jesus' enemies do the deed, but the death takes place within God's purpose.

decisions.choice: turn away from me
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what falling away means here.

decisions.choice: caer (L); tropezar y caer (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is to be tripped up so as to desert him (meaning decision m1). "Escandalizarse" today means to be shocked, which is not the sense; "tropezar y caer" keeps the picture of tripping, as the English does. The same in 14:29.

decisions.choice: mtajikwaa (L); mtajikwaa na kuanguka (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is to be tripped up so as to desert him (meaning decision m1). "Kujikwaa" keeps the picture of stumbling, as the English does; "kuchukizwa" (be offended) loses it. The same in 14:29.

source.text: ἀλλὰ μετὰ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με προάξω ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.

records.literal_gloss: But after the being raised me I will go before you into the Galilee.

en.L: But after I have been raised, I will go before you into Galilee."
en.B: But after I am raised up, I will lead the way ahead of you into Galilee."
en.R: But after God raises {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from death, I will go to Galilee before you get there."

es.L: Pero después de haber sido yo resucitado, {{plural_you:los|os}} precederé a Galilea».
es.B: Pero después de ser resucitado, iré delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a Galilea».
es.R: Pero después de que Dios {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} resucite, iré a Galilea antes que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».

sw.L: Lakini baada ya kufufuliwa {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, nitawatangulia kwenda Galilaya."
sw.B: Lakini baada ya kufufuliwa, nitawatangulia kwenda Galilaya."
sw.R: Lakini baada ya Mungu kunifufua kutoka kwa wafu, nitakwenda Galilaya kabla ninyi hamjafika huko."

decisions.choice: being raised: raised by God
decisions.reason: The verb is passive in form. In the New Testament God is the one who raises Jesus. Some take the form as simply "rise"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: go before: go ahead of, as a shepherd leads his flock
decisions.reason: After the picture of the scattered sheep, Jesus promises to gather them again. The angel at the tomb repeats the promise (16:7).

decisions.choice: God raises me from death
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who raises, as the passive implies.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἔφη αὐτῷ· Εἰ καὶ πάντες σκανδαλισθήσονται, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐγώ.

records.literal_gloss: But Peter said to him, If even all will fall away, yet not I.

en.L: But Peter said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Even if all fall away, yet not I."
en.B: Peter told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "They may all fall away, but I will not."
en.R: Peter said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "All the others may turn away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, but I never will!"

es.L: Pero Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Aunque todos caigan, yo no».
es.B: Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondió: «Puede que todos caigan, pero yo no».
es.R: Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Puede que todos los demás {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} abandonen, ¡pero yo nunca!».

sw.L: Lakini Petro akamwambia, "Hata kama wote watajikwaa, lakini si mimi."
sw.B: Petro akamwambia, "Hata kama wote watajikwaa, mimi sitajikwaa."
sw.R: Petro akamwambia, "Wengine wote wanaweza kukuacha, lakini mimi sitakuacha kamwe!"

decisions.choice: even if all ...: Peter sets himself apart from the rest
alternatives: he doubts the others will fall
decisions.reason: Peter grants that the others might fail but says he will be the exception.

decisions.choice: all the others
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Peter means the other disciples.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι σὺ σήμερον ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ πρὶν ἢ δὶς ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And says to him Jesus, Truly I say to you that you today this night before twice a rooster crows three times me you will deny.

en.L: And Jesus says to him, "Truly I say to you that you, today, this night, before a rooster crows twice, will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times."
en.B: Jesus answered him, "Truly I tell you, before a rooster crows twice today, this very night, you yourself will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times."
en.R: Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth: Tonight, before the rooster crows two times, you will say three times that you do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: Y le dice Jesús: «En verdad te digo que tú, hoy, esta noche, antes que un gallo cante dos veces, tres veces {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} negarás».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «En verdad te digo que hoy, esta misma noche, antes de que un gallo cante dos veces, tú mismo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} negarás tres veces».
es.R: Jesús le respondió: «Te digo la verdad: esta noche, antes de que el gallo cante dos veces, tú dirás tres veces que no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conoces».

sw.L: Naye Yesu anamwambia, "Kweli nakuambia kwamba wewe, leo, usiku huu, kabla jogoo hajawika mara mbili, utanikana mara tatu."
sw.B: Yesu akamjibu, "Kweli nakuambia, leo, usiku huu huu, kabla jogoo hajawika mara mbili, wewe mwenyewe utanikana mara tatu."
sw.R: Yesu akamjibu, "Nakuambia ukweli: Usiku huu, kabla jogoo hajawika mara mbili, utasema mara tatu kwamba hunijui."

decisions.choice: today, this night: the day began at sunset
decisions.reason: A Jewish day ran from evening to evening, so the night already begun was part of "today".

decisions.choice: before a rooster crows twice: before the early hours of the morning
decisions.reason: Roosters crow in the night as well as at dawn. The time of their crowing was a name for the third watch of the night (13:35).

decisions.choice: twice, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: before a rooster crows, without twice
decisions.reason: Some important early manuscripts do not have "twice", here or at 14:68 and 14:72, which brings Mark into line with the other Gospels. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: deny: disown, say he does not know Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter's three denials in 14:68-71 show what is meant: he says he does not know Jesus. Compare 8:34, where following Jesus means to deny oneself.

decisions.choice: say three times that you do not know me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the denial will be.

decisions.choice: negar (L, B); decir que no me conoces (R)
decisions.reason: To disown Jesus, saying he does not know him (meaning decision m4). "Negar" is the word used for Peter's denial in John 13:38 and Matthew 26; Readable says what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: kukana (L, B); kusema kwamba hunijui (R)
decisions.reason: To disown Jesus, saying he does not know him (meaning decision m4). "Kukana" is to deny knowing someone, the word used for Peter's denial in John 13:38 and Matthew 26; "kukataa" is to refuse or reject. Readable says what it means, as the English does.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἐκπερισσῶς ἐλάλει· Ἐὰν δέῃ με συναποθανεῖν σοι, οὐ μή σε ἀπαρνήσομαι.

records.literal_gloss: But he emphatically was saying, If it is necessary me to die with you, not not you I will deny.

en.L: But he kept saying emphatically, "If I must die with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, I will never deny {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: But Peter kept saying all the more firmly, "Should I have to die with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, still I will never deny {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: But Peter said it again and again, very strongly, "I will never say I do not know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! I will die with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} if I have to!"

es.L: Pero él decía con más insistencia: «Aunque tenga que morir contigo, de ninguna manera {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} negaré».
es.B: Pero Pedro insistía con más fuerza todavía: «Aunque tenga que morir contigo, jamás {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} negaré».
es.R: Pero Pedro lo repetía una y otra vez con mucha fuerza: «¡Nunca diré que no {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} conozco! ¡Moriré contigo si es necesario!».

sw.L: Lakini yeye alikuwa akisema kwa msisitizo mkubwa, "Hata ikinilazimu kufa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}, sitakukana kamwe."
sw.B: Lakini Petro aliendelea kusema kwa nguvu zaidi, "Hata kama itanibidi kufa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}, sitakukana kamwe."
sw.R: Lakini Petro alirudia tena na tena kwa nguvu, "Sitasema kamwe kwamba sikujui! Nitakufa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} ikibidi!"

decisions.choice: emphatically: with great force, more and more
decisions.reason: The adverb is very strong, and the verb is continuous: he kept on insisting.

decisions.choice: not not I will deny: never will I deny
decisions.reason: The double negative makes the strongest denial Greek can make.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

source.text: ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ πάντες ἔλεγον.

records.literal_gloss: Likewise and also all were saying.

en.L: And they all were also saying the same.
en.B: And every one of them said the same.
en.R: All the other followers said the same thing.

es.L: Y lo mismo decían también todos.
es.B: Y todos los demás decían lo mismo.
es.R: Todos los otros discípulos dijeron lo mismo.

sw.L: Na wote pia walikuwa wakisema vivyo hivyo.
sw.B: Na wengine wote walisema vivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Wanafunzi wengine wote nao walisema hivyo hivyo.

decisions.choice: all were saying: all the disciples said so too
decisions.reason: All of them make the promise that all will break in 14:50.

source.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς χωρίον οὗ τὸ ὄνομα Γεθσημανί, καὶ λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Καθίσατε ὧδε ἕως προσεύξωμαι.

records.literal_gloss: And they come to a place of which the name [is] Gethsemane, and he says to the disciples of him, Sit here while I pray.

en.L: And they come to a place whose name [is] Gethsemane, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Sit here while I pray."
en.B: Then they came to a place by the name of Gethsemane, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Stay seated here while I pray."
en.R: They went to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Sit here while I go and pray."

es.L: Y llegan a un lugar cuyo nombre [es] Getsemaní, y dice a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «{{plural_you:Siéntense|Sentaos}} aquí mientras oro».
es.B: Luego llegaron a un lugar llamado Getsemaní, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «{{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} sentados aquí mientras yo oro».
es.R: Fueron a un lugar llamado Getsemaní. Jesús les dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «{{plural_you:Siéntense|Sentaos}} aquí mientras yo voy a orar».
