sw.L: Na wanafika mahali ambapo jina lake [ni] Gethsemane, naye anawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Kaeni hapa wakati ninaomba."
sw.B: Kisha walifika mahali panapoitwa Gethsemane, naye akawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Kaeni hapa wakati ninapoomba."
sw.R: Walikwenda mahali panapoitwa Gethsemane. Yesu akawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Kaeni hapa wakati {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninakwenda kuomba."

decisions.choice: Gethsemane: a name meaning "oil press"
decisions.reason: The name comes from the Hebrew and Aramaic for an olive press. It was an olive grove on the Mount of Olives; John 18:1 calls it a garden.

decisions.choice: a place: a piece of land, an estate
decisions.reason: The word means a plot of ground or a small property.

decisions.choice: go and pray
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Jesus goes on a little way to pray, as 14:35 says.

source.text: καὶ παραλαμβάνει τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἤρξατο ἐκθαμβεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου· μείνατε ὧδε καὶ γρηγορεῖτε.

records.literal_gloss: And he takes Peter and James and John with him, and he began to be greatly alarmed and to be distressed, \v 34 and he says to them, Very sorrowful is the soul of me to death; remain here and keep watch.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes Peter and James and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to be greatly alarmed and distressed, \v 34 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "My soul is very sorrowful, even to death. Remain here and keep watch."
en.B: He took Peter, James and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and horror and anguish came over {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 34 He said to them, "My soul is filled with grief, grief enough to die. Wait here and stay awake."
en.R: Jesus took Peter, James and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He began to feel great fear and deep pain. \v 34 He said to them, "My heart is so full of sorrow that I feel as if I am dying. Stay here and keep watch."

es.L: Y toma consigo a Pedro, a Santiago y a Juan, y comenzó a sentirse sobrecogido y angustiado, \v 34 y les dice: «Llena de tristeza está {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} alma, hasta la muerte; {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} aquí y {{plural_you:velen|velad}}».
es.B: Se llevó consigo a Pedro, a Santiago y a Juan, y el espanto y la angustia se apoderaron de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. \v 34 Les dijo: «Siento en el alma una tristeza de muerte. {{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} aquí y {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} despiertos».
es.R: Jesús llevó consigo a Pedro, a Santiago y a Juan. Comenzó a sentir mucho miedo y un dolor muy profundo. \v 34 Les dijo: «Siento tanta tristeza en el corazón que es como si estuviera a punto de morir. {{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} aquí y {{plural_you:estén|estad}} atentos».

sw.L: Naye anawachukua Petro na Yakobo na Yohana pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, akaanza kushikwa na hofu kuu na kuhangaika sana, \v 34 naye anawaambia, "Nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} imejaa huzuni hata kufa; bakini hapa na mkae macho."
sw.B: Aliwachukua Petro, Yakobo na Yohana pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, na hofu kuu na dhiki zikamwingia. \v 34 Akawaambia, "Nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} imelemewa na huzuni, huzuni inayoweza kuniua. Bakini hapa, mkae macho."
sw.R: Yesu aliwachukua Petro, Yakobo na Yohana pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}. Akaanza kuogopa sana na kuumia moyoni. \v 34 Akawaambia, "Moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} umejaa huzuni nyingi mno, hata najiona kama ninakufa. Bakini hapa mkae macho."

decisions.choice: greatly alarmed and distressed: overwhelmed with horror and anguish
decisions.reason: The first verb is the strong word for being overwhelmed used in 9:15 and 16:5-6. The second means to be in deep distress. Together they show Jesus in agony as he faces his death.

decisions.choice: my soul is very sorrowful: words from Psalms 42 and 43
decisions.reason: The refrain "Why are you cast down, my soul?" (Psalm 42:6, 42:12; 43:5) uses this word in the Greek version. Jesus prays in the words of a psalm of distress.

decisions.choice: even to death: sorrow so great it could kill
decisions.reason: The phrase measures the grief: it is deep enough to bring death (compare Jonah 4:9).

decisions.choice: keep watch: stay awake and alert
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 13:34-37 for servants who must stay awake for their master's coming.

decisions.choice: My heart is so full of sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for the inner self.

decisions.choice: Siento en el alma una tristeza de muerte (B); siento tanta tristeza en el corazón (R)
alternatives: Mi alma está muy triste, hasta la muerte
decisions.reason: Sorrow so great it could kill (meaning decision m3). Balanced says it as a Spanish speaker would, and avoids the wording of the familiar Spanish Bibles; Readable says "corazón" for the English "heart".

decisions.choice: Nafsi yangu (L, B); Moyo wangu (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus's inner self (meaning decision m2). "Nafsi" is the self that feels; "roho" is also the word for "spirit", which 14:38 sets against the flesh. Readable says "moyo" for the English "heart".

source.text: καὶ προελθὼν μικρὸν ἔπιπτεν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ προσηύχετο ἵνα εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν παρέλθῃ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἡ ὥρα, καὶ ἔλεγεν· Αββα ὁ πατήρ, πάντα δυνατά σοι· παρένεγκε τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ· ἀλλ’ οὐ τί ἐγὼ θέλω ἀλλὰ τί σύ.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone forward a little he was falling on the ground and was praying that if possible it is might pass from him the hour, \v 36 and he was saying, Abba, the Father, all things [are] possible to you; take away the cup this from me; but not what I will but what you.

en.L: And going forward a little, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was falling on the ground and praying that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 36 And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying, "Abba, Father, all things [are] possible for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Take this cup away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; but not what I will, but what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [will]."
en.B: He went on a little way, threw {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to the ground and prayed that the hour might pass {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by, if that could be. \v 36 He said, "Abba, Father, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all things are possible. Remove this cup from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Yet let it be what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will, not what I will."
en.R: Jesus went a short way farther. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fell to the ground and prayed. He asked that, if it could happen, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not have to go through this time of suffering. \v 36 He said, "Abba, Father, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can do anything. Please take this cup of suffering away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, not what I want."

es.L: Y yendo un poco más adelante, caía en tierra y oraba que, si era posible, pasara de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} la hora. \v 36 Y decía: «Abba, Padre, todo [es] posible para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}; aleja esta copa de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; pero no lo que yo quiero, sino lo que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} [quieres]».
es.B: Se adelantó un poco, se echó en tierra y oraba que, si era posible, aquella hora pasara lejos de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. \v 36 Decía: «Abba, Padre, para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} todo es posible. Aleja de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} esta copa. Pero que se haga lo que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quieres, no lo que quiero yo».
es.R: Jesús se alejó un poco más. Allí se tiró al suelo y oró. Pidió que, si era posible, no tuviera que pasar por ese tiempo de sufrimiento. \v 36 Decía: «Abba, Padre, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} puedes hacerlo todo. Por favor, quítame esta copa de sufrimiento. Pero haz lo que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quieres, no lo que quiero yo».

sw.L: Na akienda mbele kidogo, alikuwa akianguka chini, na akiomba kwamba, ikiwezekana, saa hiyo impite. \v 36 Naye alikuwa akisema, "Aba, Baba, vitu vyote [vinawezekana] {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}; kiondoe kikombe hiki {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}; lakini si kile ninachotaka {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, bali kile unachotaka {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}."
sw.B: Akaenda mbele kidogo, akajitupa chini, akaomba kwamba, kama ingewezekana, saa hiyo imwepuke. \v 36 Akasema, "Aba, Baba, {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}} kila kitu kinawezekana. Kiondoe kikombe hiki {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}. Lakini na kifanyike unachotaka {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, si ninachotaka {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}."
sw.R: Yesu alikwenda mbele kidogo. Huko alianguka chini, akaomba. Aliomba kwamba, kama ingewezekana, asipitie wakati huo wa mateso. \v 36 Akasema, "Aba, Baba, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unaweza kufanya kila kitu. Tafadhali niondolee kikombe hiki cha mateso. Lakini fanya {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unachotaka, si ninachotaka {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}."

decisions.choice: was falling ... was praying ... was saying: prayer that went on
decisions.reason: The verbs are continuous. Jesus prayed this way again and again (14:39).

decisions.choice: Abba, Father: the Aramaic word for father, with its Greek meaning
decisions.reason: Abba was the word a son or daughter used for their father, at any age. Mark keeps it and adds the Greek word. Paul says that believers too cry "Abba, Father" (Romans 8:15; Galatians 4:6).

decisions.choice: the hour; this cup: the suffering and death now upon him
decisions.reason: The cup is a picture from the prophets of God's judgment that must be drunk (Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15). Jesus used it in 10:38-39. The hour is the time of his betrayal and death (14:41).

decisions.choice: not what I will but what you will: Jesus gives his will over to the Father's
decisions.reason: Jesus asks for the cup to be taken away, but puts the Father's will first. He does what he taught in 3:35 and 8:34.

decisions.choice: this time of suffering; this cup of suffering
decisions.reason: Readable says what the hour and the cup stand for.

decisions.choice: Abba, Padre
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word for father, followed by its Greek meaning (meaning decision m2). Spanish keeps the Aramaic word, as Romans 8:15 does, so that the reader sees Jesus's own word; "Papá" would make it sound childish.

decisions.choice: Aba, Baba
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word for father, followed by its Greek meaning (meaning decision m2). Swahili keeps the Aramaic word, as Romans 8:15 does, so that the reader sees Jesus's own word.

source.text: καὶ ἔρχεται καὶ εὑρίσκει αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, καὶ λέγει τῷ Πέτρῳ· Σίμων, καθεύδεις;

records.literal_gloss: And he comes and finds them sleeping, and he says to Peter, Simon, are you sleeping?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes and finds them sleeping, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to Peter, "Simon, are you sleeping?
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back and found them asleep. He said to Peter, "Simon, are you asleep?
en.R: Then Jesus came back and found the three followers asleep. He said to Peter, "Simon, are you sleeping?

es.L: Y viene y los encuentra durmiendo, y dice a Pedro: «Simón, ¿duermes?
es.B: Luego volvió y los encontró dormidos. Le dijo a Pedro: «Simón, ¿estás dormido?
es.R: Luego Jesús volvió y encontró dormidos a los tres discípulos. Le dijo a Pedro: «Simón, ¿estás durmiendo?

sw.L: Naye anakuja na kuwakuta wamelala, naye anamwambia Petro, "Simoni, unalala?
sw.B: Kisha alirudi, akawakuta wamelala usingizi. Akamwambia Petro, "Simoni, umelala?
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alirudi, akawakuta wale wanafunzi watatu wamelala. Akamwambia Petro, "Simoni, umelala?

decisions.choice: Simon: Peter's own name, not the name Jesus gave him
alternatives: no meaning in the change of name
decisions.reason: Since 3:16 Mark has called him Peter. Jesus now uses his old name. Some see a hint that he is not living up to his new name; Mark does not say.

decisions.choice: comes, finds, says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: the three followers
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the three of 14:33 are meant.

source.text: οὐκ ἴσχυσας μίαν ὥραν γρηγορῆσαι;

records.literal_gloss: Not were you strong one hour to keep watch?

en.L: Were you not strong enough to keep watch one hour?
en.B: Did you not have the strength to stay awake a single hour?
en.R: Could you not stay awake for just one hour?

es.L: ¿No tuviste fuerza para velar una hora?
es.B: ¿No has tenido fuerzas para mantenerte despierto ni una sola hora?
es.R: ¿No pudiste quedarte despierto ni siquiera una hora?

sw.L: Hukuwa na nguvu ya kukesha saa moja?
sw.B: Hukuwa na nguvu za kukaa macho hata saa moja tu?
sw.R: Hukuweza kukaa macho hata kwa saa moja tu?

decisions.choice: were you strong: you, Peter alone
decisions.reason: The verb is singular. Peter, who had promised so much (14:29-31), could not stay awake for one hour.

decisions.choice: strong: able, having the strength
decisions.reason: The verb means to have strength for something.

source.text: γρηγορεῖτε καὶ προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ ἔλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν· τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής.

records.literal_gloss: Keep watch and pray, so that not you come into temptation; the indeed spirit [is] willing, but the flesh weak.

en.L: Keep watch and pray, so that you may not come into temptation; the spirit indeed [is] willing, but the flesh [is] weak."
en.B: Stay awake and pray that you will not come into temptation. The spirit is eager, but the flesh is weak."
en.R: Stay awake and pray. Then you will not give in when temptation comes. Your spirit wants to do what is right, but your body is weak."

es.L: {{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} en vela y {{plural_you:oren|orad}}, para que no {{plural_you:vengan|vengáis}} a tentación; el espíritu, en efecto, [está] dispuesto, pero la carne [es] débil».
es.B: {{plural_you:Manténganse|Manteneos}} despiertos y {{plural_you:oren|orad}} para no caer en la tentación. El espíritu está deseoso, pero la carne es débil».
es.R: {{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} despiertos y {{plural_you:oren|orad}}. Así no {{plural_you:cederán|cederéis}} cuando venga la tentación. {{plural_you:El espíritu de ustedes|Vuestro espíritu}} quiere hacer lo correcto, pero {{plural_you:su cuerpo|vuestro cuerpo}} es débil».

sw.L: Kaeni macho na kuomba, ili msiingie katika majaribu; roho kwa kweli [ina] nia, lakini mwili [ni] dhaifu."
sw.B: Kaeni macho mwombe, ili msiangukie majaribuni. Roho ina hamu, lakini mwili ni dhaifu."
sw.R: Kaeni macho na mwombe. Ndipo hamtashindwa wakati majaribu yatakapokuja. Roho zenu zinataka kufanya lililo sawa, lakini miili yenu ni dhaifu."

decisions.choice: keep watch and pray: now spoken to all three
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural. Jesus turns from Peter to all of them.

decisions.choice: temptation: a time of testing that could lead them to fall
alternatives: an inward desire for something wrong only
decisions.reason: The word means a test or trial. The arrest is about to test them, and they will fall (14:50). Compare the prayer "lead us not into temptation" (Matthew 6:13).

decisions.choice: the spirit and the flesh: the willing human spirit and weak human nature
decisions.reason: The spirit here is the inner self that wants to do right; the flesh is human nature in its weakness. Some take the spirit as God's Spirit, but the contrast is within the person.

decisions.choice: your spirit wants to do what is right; your body
alternatives: the spirit is willing; the flesh
decisions.reason: Readable explains the saying in plain words.

decisions.choice: majaribu
decisions.reason: A time of testing that could lead them to fall (meaning decision m2). "Majaribu" covers both the testing and the pull to give in; "kishawishi" is only an enticement to sin.

source.text: καὶ πάλιν ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπών.

records.literal_gloss: And again having gone away he prayed the same word having said.

en.L: And again going away, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prayed, saying the same word.
en.B: He went away again and prayed, using the same words.
en.R: Jesus went away again and prayed the same prayer.

es.L: Y yéndose otra vez, oró, diciendo la misma palabra.
es.B: Se alejó otra vez y oró con las mismas palabras.
es.R: Jesús se fue otra vez e hizo la misma oración.

sw.L: Na tena akienda zake, aliomba, akisema neno lile lile.
sw.B: Akaenda tena, akaomba kwa maneno yale yale.
sw.R: Yesu alikwenda tena, akaomba ombi lile lile.

decisions.choice: the same word: the same request
decisions.reason: The word can mean a saying or a matter. Jesus prayed the same prayer as before.

source.text: καὶ πάλιν ἐλθὼν εὗρεν αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, ἦσαν γὰρ αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ καταβαρυνόμενοι, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδεισαν τί ἀποκριθῶσιν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And again having come he found them sleeping, were for of them the eyes being weighed down, and not they knew what they might answer him.

en.L: And again coming, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down, and they did not know what they should answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Coming back again, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them asleep; they could not keep their eyes open, and they had no answer to give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus came back to them again. Once more {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them sleeping. They were too tired to keep their eyes open. They did not know what to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y volviendo otra vez, los encontró durmiendo, pues sus ojos estaban cargados, y no sabían qué {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} iban a responder.
es.B: Cuando volvió de nuevo, los encontró dormidos; no podían mantener los ojos abiertos, y no sabían qué {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} podían responder.
es.R: Jesús volvió otra vez adonde estaban ellos. Otra vez los encontró dormidos. Estaban tan cansados que no podían tener los ojos abiertos. No sabían qué {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} podían decir.

sw.L: Na alipokuja tena, aliwakuta wamelala, kwa maana macho yao yalikuwa mazito, wala hawakujua watakalomjibu.
sw.B: Aliporudi tena, aliwakuta wamelala; hawakuweza kuyaweka macho yao wazi, na hawakuwa na jibu la kumpa.
sw.R: Yesu aliwarudia tena. Tena aliwakuta wamelala. Walikuwa wamechoka mno hata hawakuweza kufumbua macho. Hawakujua la kumwambia.

decisions.choice: eyes weighed down: very drowsy
decisions.reason: The phrase means they were heavy with sleep.

decisions.choice: did not know what to answer: they were ashamed and had nothing to say
decisions.reason: As on the mountain in 9:6, the disciples are at a loss for words.

source.text: καὶ ἔρχεται τὸ τρίτον καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Καθεύδετε τὸ λοιπὸν καὶ ἀναπαύεσθε· ἀπέχει· ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα, ἰδοὺ παραδίδοται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰς τὰς χεῖρας τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And he comes the third [time] and says to them, Are you sleeping the rest and resting? It is enough; came the hour, look, is handed over the Son of Man into the hands of the sinners.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes the third [time] and says to them, "Are you still sleeping and resting? It is enough. The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
en.B: He came a third time and said to them, "Still asleep? Still resting? Enough of that! The hour is here. See, the Son of Man is being handed over into the power of sinners.
en.R: Jesus came back a third time and said to them, "Are you still asleep and resting? That is enough! The time is here. Look! The Son of Man is being handed over to sinful people.

es.L: Y viene la tercera [vez] y les dice: «¿Todavía {{plural_you:duermen|dormís}} y {{plural_you:descansan|descansáis}}? Basta; ha llegado la hora; {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, el Hijo del Hombre es entregado en manos de los pecadores.
es.B: Vino por tercera vez y les dijo: «¿Todavía {{plural_you:duermen|dormís}}? ¿Todavía {{plural_you:descansan|descansáis}}? ¡Basta ya! Ha llegado la hora. {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, el Hijo del Hombre está siendo entregado en poder de los pecadores.
es.R: Jesús volvió por tercera vez y les dijo: «¿Todavía {{plural_you:están|estáis}} durmiendo y descansando? ¡Ya basta! Ha llegado el momento. ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! El Hijo del Hombre está siendo entregado a gente pecadora.

sw.L: Naye anakuja mara ya tatu na kuwaambia, "Je, bado mnalala na kupumzika? Inatosha; saa imefika; tazameni, Mwana wa Adamu anakabidhiwa mikononi mwa wenye dhambi.
sw.B: Akaja mara ya tatu, akawaambia, "Bado mnalala? Bado mnapumzika? Basi! Saa imefika. Tazameni, Mwana wa Adamu anatiwa mikononi mwa wenye dhambi.
sw.R: Yesu alirudi mara ya tatu, akawaambia, "Bado mnalala na kupumzika? Inatosha! Wakati umefika. Tazameni! Mwana wa Adamu anakabidhiwa kwa watu wenye dhambi.

decisions.choice: Are you still sleeping and resting?: a question
alternatives: Sleep on now and take your rest (a command)
decisions.reason: The same words can be read as a command, said with sorrow or irony: "Sleep on, then." But the next words wake them up, so a question fits better.

decisions.choice: it is enough: that is enough, the time for sleep is over
decisions.reason: The word is unclear here. In business it meant "paid in full", and some take it of Judas receiving his money. The most common reading is "enough!". Some manuscripts add words to explain it.

decisions.choice: handed over: given up by God's plan, through Judas's betrayal
decisions.reason: This is the word of Jesus' sayings about his death (9:31; 10:33). Here it covers both what Judas does and what God allows.

decisions.choice: sinners: those who act against God, here his enemies
decisions.reason: The word may point to the Gentiles who will kill him (10:33), but the arresting crowd comes from the Jewish leaders.

decisions.choice: into the power of
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the idiom.

source.text: ἐγείρεσθε ἄγωμεν· ἰδοὺ ὁ παραδιδούς με ἤγγικεν.

records.literal_gloss: Rise, let us go; look, the [one] handing over me has drawn near.

en.L: Rise, let us go. Look, the one who is handing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over has drawn near."
en.B: Get up; we must go. Look, the one who betrays {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is near."
en.R: Get up! Let us go. Look! The man who is betraying {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is almost here."

es.L: {{plural_you:Levántense|Levantaos}}, vamos; {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} entrega se ha acercado».
es.B: {{plural_you:Levántense|Levantaos}}; tenemos que irnos. {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, ya está cerca el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} traiciona».
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Levántense|Levantaos}}! Vámonos. ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! Ya casi está aquí el hombre que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} traiciona».

sw.L: Amkeni, twendeni; tazameni, yeye anayenikabidhi amekaribia."
sw.B: Inukeni, twende zetu. Tazameni, anayenisaliti yuko karibu."
sw.R: Amkeni! Twendeni. Tazameni! Mtu anayenisaliti karibu atafika hapa."

decisions.choice: let us go: let us go to meet them
decisions.reason: Jesus does not flee. He goes out to meet those who come for him.

decisions.choice: has drawn near: is here
decisions.reason: The perfect means he has come near and is now at hand, as in 1:15.

decisions.choice: the one who betrays (B); the man who is betraying (R)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, Balanced and Readable name Judas's act as betrayal.

source.text: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος παραγίνεται Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα καὶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄχλος μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately, yet him speaking, arrives Judas one of the Twelve and with him a crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.

en.L: And immediately, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrives, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
en.B: Right then, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still talking, Judas came up, one of the Twelve. A crowd came with him carrying swords and clubs. They had been sent by the chief priests, the scribes and the elders.
en.R: Just then, while Jesus was still speaking, Judas arrived. He was one of the twelve followers. A crowd came with him. They had swords and heavy sticks. The leading priests, the teachers of God's law, and the elders had sent them.

es.L: Y en seguida, mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} todavía hablaba, llega Judas, uno de los Doce, y con él una multitud con espadas y palos, de parte de los jefes de los sacerdotes y de los escribas y de los ancianos.
es.B: En ese mismo instante, mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} todavía hablaba, llegó Judas, uno de los Doce. Con él venía una multitud armada con espadas y palos. Los enviaban los jefes de los sacerdotes, los escribas y los ancianos.
es.R: En ese momento, mientras Jesús todavía hablaba, llegó Judas. Era uno de los doce discípulos. Con él venía una multitud. Traían espadas y garrotes. Los habían enviado los jefes de los sacerdotes, los maestros de la ley y los ancianos.

sw.L: Na mara, alipokuwa bado akisema, anafika Yuda, mmoja wa wale Kumi na Wawili, na pamoja naye umati wa watu wakiwa na panga na virungu, kutoka kwa wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi na wazee.
sw.B: Papo hapo, alipokuwa bado anazungumza, Yuda, mmoja wa wale Kumi na Wawili, alifika. Umati wa watu ulikuja pamoja naye, wakibeba panga na virungu. Walikuwa wametumwa na wakuu wa makuhani, waandishi na wazee.
sw.R: Wakati huo huo, Yesu alipokuwa bado anasema, Yuda alifika. Yeye alikuwa mmoja wa wanafunzi kumi na wawili. Umati wa watu ulikuja pamoja naye. Walikuwa na panga na fimbo nzito. Wakuu wa makuhani, walimu wa sheria na wazee walikuwa wamewatuma.

decisions.choice: a crowd ... from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders: men sent by the council
decisions.reason: The three groups make up the council of 14:53-55. Those sent were likely the temple guard and servants of the high priest (14:47).

decisions.choice: one of the Twelve: Mark repeats it
decisions.reason: Mark names him again in this way (as in 14:10 and 14:20) to stress that the betrayer was one of Jesus' own.

decisions.choice: clubs: wooden staves
decisions.reason: The word means wood and is used of clubs or cudgels.

decisions.choice: right then (B); just then (R)
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, Literal says "immediately" and the other levels vary the phrase.

source.text: δεδώκει δὲ ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν σύσσημον αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὃν ἂν φιλήσω αὐτός ἐστιν· κρατήσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἀπάγετε ἀσφαλῶς.

records.literal_gloss: Had given now the [one] handing over him a signal to them saying, Whomever I kiss, he is; seize him and lead away securely.

en.L: Now the one who was handing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over had given them a signal, saying, "Whomever I kiss, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is [the one]; seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and lead [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] away under guard."
en.B: Judas, the betrayer, had given them a signal beforehand. "The one I kiss is {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}," he had said. "Take hold of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and lead {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away under close guard."
en.R: Judas had told them ahead of time how they would know which man was Jesus. He said, "The man I kiss is the one you want. Grab {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away. Guard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} well."

es.L: Y el que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregaba les había dado una señal, diciendo: «Al que yo bese, ese es; {{plural_you:préndanlo|prendedlo}} y {{plural_you:llévenlo|llevadlo}} bien custodiado».
es.B: Judas, el traidor, les había dado de antemano una señal: «Al que yo bese, ese es», les había dicho. «{{plural_you:Agárrenlo|Agarradlo}} y {{plural_you:llévenselo|lleváoslo}} bien vigilado».
es.R: Judas les había dicho antes cómo iban a saber cuál de los hombres era Jesús. Les dijo: «El hombre al que yo bese es el que {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}. {{plural_you:Agárrenlo|Agarradlo}} y {{plural_you:llévenselo|lleváoslo}}. {{plural_you:Vigílenlo|Vigiladlo}} bien».

sw.L: Na yule aliyekuwa akimkabidhi alikuwa amewapa ishara, akisema, "Nitakayembusu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye; mkamateni na kumpeleka chini ya ulinzi."
sw.B: Yuda, msaliti, alikuwa amewapa ishara mapema: "Nitakayembusu ndiye {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}," alikuwa amesema. "Mkamateni, mumpeleke chini ya ulinzi mkali."
sw.R: Yuda alikuwa amewaambia mapema jinsi watakavyomtambua Yesu. Alisema, "Mtu nitakayembusu ndiye mnayemtafuta. Mkamateni, mumchukue. Mlindeni vizuri."

decisions.choice: kiss: the usual greeting of a disciple to his teacher
decisions.reason: A kiss was a common greeting of respect. Judas turns that greeting into a signal, and in the dark the crowd needs to know which man to take.

decisions.choice: securely: under guard, so that he does not escape
decisions.reason: The word can mean safely or securely. Judas wants to make sure Jesus is held.

decisions.choice: signal: an agreed sign between people
decisions.reason: The word means a token agreed beforehand.

decisions.choice: Judas, the betrayer, had given them a signal beforehand
alternatives: the one handing him over had given them a signal
decisions.reason: Balanced names Judas and makes clear the signal was arranged in advance, as the past perfect implies.

source.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν εὐθὺς προσελθὼν αὐτῷ λέγει· Ῥαββί, καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And having come immediately having approached him he says, Rabbi, and kissed him.

en.L: And coming, immediately approaching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, he says, "Rabbi," and kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: As soon as he arrived, he went straight up to Jesus and said, "Rabbi!" and kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Judas came and went straight to Jesus. He said, "Teacher!" and kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y llegando, en seguida, acercándose a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, dice: «Rabí», y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} besó.
es.B: Apenas llegó, se acercó directamente a Jesús, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «¡Rabí!», y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} besó.
es.R: Judas llegó y fue directamente hacia Jesús. Le dijo: «¡Maestro!», y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} besó.

sw.L: Na alipofika, mara akimwendea, anasema, "Rabi," akambusu.
sw.B: Mara alipofika, alimwendea Yesu moja kwa moja, akasema, "Rabi!" akambusu.
sw.R: Yuda alifika, akamwendea Yesu moja kwa moja. Akasema, "Mwalimu!" akambusu.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: my teacher, a respectful title
decisions.reason: Judas greets Jesus with the title of honor a disciple used for his teacher (9:5; 11:21).

decisions.choice: kissed: the stronger form of the verb
decisions.reason: The verb is a compound of the one in 14:44. It may mean he kissed him warmly, which makes the betrayal worse, or it may simply mean kissed.

decisions.choice: Teacher
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, Readable says "Teacher" for Rabbi.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐπέβαλαν τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ καὶ ἐκράτησαν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And they laid the hands on him and seized him.

en.L: And they laid hands on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and seized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: They then laid hands on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} prisoner.
en.R: Then the men grabbed Jesus and arrested {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} echaron las manos y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} prendieron.
es.B: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} echaron mano y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} tomaron preso.
es.R: Entonces los hombres agarraron a Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} arrestaron.

sw.L: Nao wakanyosha mikono yao juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wakamkamata.
sw.B: Basi wakamshika kwa nguvu, wakamtia nguvuni.
sw.R: Kisha wale watu walimshika Yesu, wakamkamata.

decisions.choice: laid hands on: took hold of by force
decisions.reason: Here laying on hands is an arrest, not a blessing.

source.text: εἷς δέ τις τῶν παρεστηκότων σπασάμενος τὴν μάχαιραν ἔπαισεν τὸν δοῦλον τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ ἀφεῖλεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτάριον.

records.literal_gloss: One but a certain of those standing by, having drawn the sword, struck the slave of the high priest and took off of him the ear.

en.L: But a certain one of those standing by drew his sword, struck the slave of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
en.B: But one of the bystanders pulled out his sword, hit the high priest's servant and cut off his ear.
en.R: One of the people standing there pulled out a sword. He swung it at the high priest's servant and cut off his ear.

es.L: Pero uno de los que estaban allí, sacando la espada, hirió al esclavo del sumo sacerdote y le cortó la oreja.
es.B: Pero uno de los que estaban presentes desenvainó la espada, golpeó al siervo del sumo sacerdote y le cortó la oreja.
es.R: Uno de los que estaban allí sacó una espada. La lanzó contra el siervo del sumo sacerdote y le cortó la oreja.

sw.L: Lakini mmoja wa wale waliosimama karibu, akiuchomoa upanga, alimpiga mtumwa wa kuhani mkuu, akamkata sikio lake.
sw.B: Lakini mmoja wa watu waliokuwa wamesimama pale aliuchomoa upanga wake, akampiga mtumishi wa kuhani mkuu, akamkata sikio.
sw.R: Mmoja wa watu waliosimama pale alichomoa upanga. Akampiga nao mtumishi wa kuhani mkuu, akamkata sikio.

decisions.choice: a certain one of those standing by: Mark does not name him
decisions.reason: John 18:10 names Peter and the slave, Malchus. Mark leaves him unnamed. He seems to be one of Jesus' followers.

decisions.choice: slave: one owned by the high priest, here likely one of his trusted men
decisions.reason: The word means a slave. A high priest's slave could hold a position of trust.

decisions.choice: ear: the whole ear or the earlobe
decisions.reason: The word is a small form of the word for ear, but such forms were often used with no sense of smallness.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: esclavo (L); siervo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The man was the high priest's slave, here likely one of his trusted men (meaning decision m2). Literal says "esclavo"; Balanced and Readable say "siervo", as the English says "servant", following the term used for doulos throughout the Gospels.

decisions.choice: mtumwa (L); mtumishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The man was the high priest's slave, here likely one of his trusted men (meaning decision m2). Literal says "mtumwa"; Balanced and Readable say "mtumishi", as the English says "servant", following the term used for doulos throughout the Gospels.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων συλλαβεῖν με;

records.literal_gloss: And answering Jesus said to them, As against a bandit did you come out with swords and clubs to capture me?

en.L: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Have you come out with swords and clubs to capture {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as against a bandit?
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Have you come with swords and clubs to seize {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as you would a bandit?
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Do you think I am a robber? Is that why you came with swords and clubs to arrest {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

es.L: Y respondiendo Jesús, les dijo: «¿Como contra un bandido {{plural_you:han salido|habéis salido}} con espadas y palos para apresarme?
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «¿Con espadas y palos {{plural_you:han venido|habéis venido}} a apresarme, como si fuera un bandido?
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «¿Acaso {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} que soy un bandido? ¿Por eso {{plural_you:vinieron|vinisteis}} con espadas y garrotes para arrestarme?

sw.L: Naye Yesu akajibu, akawaambia, "Kama juu ya jambazi mmetoka na panga na virungu kunikamata?
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Mmekuja na panga na virungu kunikamata, kana kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni jambazi?
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Mnadhani {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni jambazi? Ndiyo sababu mmekuja na panga na virungu kunikamata?

decisions.choice: bandit: a robber or armed rebel
alternatives: a thief who steals in secret
decisions.reason: The word is used of violent robbers and of rebels against Rome. Jesus is crucified between two of them (15:27).

decisions.choice: a question
alternatives: a statement: you have come out as against a bandit
decisions.reason: The sentence can be read as a statement or a question. Read either way, Jesus protests at the way they treat him.

decisions.choice: Do you think I am a robber? Is that why ...?
alternatives: As against a bandit did you come out ...?
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question in two to make the point clear.

decisions.choice: bandido
decisions.reason: A robber or armed rebel (meaning decision m1). "Bandido" is a man of violence, as the swords and clubs imply; "ladrón" is a thief, which is too mild. Readable keeps "bandido" for the English "robber".

decisions.choice: jambazi
decisions.reason: A robber or armed rebel (meaning decision m1). "Jambazi" is a violent armed robber, as the swords and clubs imply; "mwizi" is a thief, which is too mild. Readable keeps "jambazi" for the English "robber".

source.text: καθ’ ἡμέραν ἤμην πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με· ἀλλ’ ἵνα πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαί.

records.literal_gloss: Every day I was with you in the temple teaching, and not you seized me; but so that may be fulfilled the Scriptures.

en.L: Every day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; but [this has happened] so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled."
en.B: Day after day I was among you in the temple, teaching, and you did not lay a hand on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But this is happening so that the Scriptures would be fulfilled."
en.R: Day after day I taught in the temple area, right there with you. You did not arrest {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} then. But all this is happening to make the Scriptures come true."

es.L: Cada día estaba con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en el templo enseñando, y no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:prendieron|prendisteis}}; pero [esto sucede] para que se cumplan las Escrituras».
es.B: Día tras día estaba entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en el templo, enseñando, y no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:pusieron|pusisteis}} la mano encima. Pero esto sucede para que se cumplan las Escrituras».
es.R: Día tras día yo enseñaba en el templo, allí mismo con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Entonces no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:arrestaron|arrestasteis}}. Pero todo esto está pasando para que se cumpla lo que dicen las Escrituras».

sw.L: Kila siku nilikuwa pamoja nanyi hekaluni nikifundisha, wala hamkunikamata; lakini [haya yametokea] ili Maandiko yatimizwe."
sw.B: Siku kwa siku nilikuwa kati yenu hekaluni, nikifundisha, wala hamkuninyooshea mkono. Lakini haya yanatokea ili Maandiko yatimie."
sw.R: Siku baada ya siku nilifundisha hekaluni, pale pale pamoja nanyi. Hamkunikamata wakati huo. Lakini mambo haya yote yanatokea ili Maandiko yatimie."

decisions.choice: but so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled: words are left out
alternatives: Let the Scriptures be fulfilled (a command)
decisions.reason: The sentence is cut short. It may mean "this has happened so that ..." or work as a wish: "let the Scriptures be fulfilled." The sense is the same: these events are in God's plan.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures: such as Zechariah 13:7 and Isaiah 53:12
decisions.reason: Jesus does not name a passage. He quoted Zechariah 13:7 in 14:27, and Isaiah 53:12 says the servant was counted with rebels.

decisions.choice: the temple: the temple courts, where he taught in 11:27-12:44
decisions.reason: Jesus taught in the open courts of the temple area.

source.text: καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἔφυγον πάντες.

records.literal_gloss: And having left him they fled all.

en.L: And leaving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they all fled.
en.B: And they all left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and ran.
en.R: Then all of Jesus' followers left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and ran away.

es.L: Y dejándolo, huyeron todos.
es.B: Y todos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} abandonaron y huyeron.
es.R: Entonces todos los discípulos de Jesús {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} dejaron solo y huyeron.

sw.L: Na wakimwacha, wote walikimbia.
sw.B: Wote walimwacha, wakatoroka.
sw.R: Kisha wanafunzi wote wa Yesu walimwacha, wakakimbia.

decisions.choice: they all fled: what Jesus foretold in 14:27
decisions.reason: The sheep are scattered as Zechariah 13:7 said, and the "all" who promised in 14:31 all run.

decisions.choice: all of Jesus' followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who fled.

source.text: Καὶ νεανίσκος τις συνηκολούθει αὐτῷ περιβεβλημένος σινδόνα ἐπὶ γυμνοῦ, καὶ κρατοῦσιν αὐτόν, ὁ δὲ καταλιπὼν τὴν σινδόνα γυμνὸς ἔφυγεν.

records.literal_gloss: And a young man certain was following with him, having wrapped a linen cloth around [his] naked [body], and they seize him; \v 52 but having left behind the linen cloth naked he fled.

en.L: And a certain young man was following with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, having wrapped a linen cloth around [his] naked [body], and they seize him; \v 52 but leaving behind the linen cloth, he fled naked.
en.B: A certain young man had been going along with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, with only a linen sheet thrown around his bare body. They seized him, \v 52 but he slipped out of the linen sheet and ran away naked.
en.R: A young man was following Jesus. He was wearing only a linen cloth. The men grabbed him. \v 52 But he left the cloth in their hands and ran away with no clothes on.

es.L: Y un joven {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} iba siguiendo, envuelto en una sábana de lino sobre el [cuerpo] desnudo, y lo prenden; \v 52 pero él, dejando la sábana, huyó desnudo.
es.B: Un joven {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} venía siguiendo, cubierto solo con una sábana de lino sobre el cuerpo desnudo. Lo agarraron, \v 52 pero él se escapó de la sábana y huyó desnudo.
es.R: Un joven iba siguiendo a Jesús. Solo llevaba puesta una tela de lino. Los hombres lo agarraron. \v 52 Pero él les dejó la tela en las manos y se escapó corriendo sin ropa.

sw.L: Na kijana mmoja alikuwa akimfuata, amejifunika shuka ya kitani juu ya [mwili] mtupu, nao wanamkamata; \v 52 lakini yeye akiiacha ile shuka, alikimbia uchi.
sw.B: Kijana mmoja alikuwa akimfuata, akiwa amejifunika shuka ya kitani tu mwilini. Wakamkamata, \v 52 lakini akaiacha shuka hiyo, akakimbia uchi.
sw.R: Kijana mmoja alikuwa akimfuata Yesu. Alikuwa amevaa kitambaa cha kitani tu. Wale watu walimkamata. \v 52 Lakini aliwaachia kitambaa hicho mikononi mwao, akakimbia bila nguo.

decisions.choice: a certain young man: Mark does not say who he was
decisions.reason: Only Mark tells this. Some have guessed the young man was Mark, but the text gives no name and there is no evidence.

decisions.choice: fled naked: possibly an echo of Amos 2:16
decisions.reason: Amos says that on the day of judgment even the bravest will flee away naked. Whether Mark had this in mind is not certain; the scene shows that even the last follower fled.

decisions.choice: linen cloth: a sheet or wrap of linen
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the cloth in which Jesus is buried (15:46).

decisions.choice: they seize: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present; the sense is past.

source.text: Καὶ ἀπήγαγον τὸν Ἰησοῦν πρὸς τὸν ἀρχιερέα, καὶ συνέρχονται πάντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And they led away Jesus to the high priest, and come together all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes.

en.L: And they led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes come together.
en.B: Jesus was led off to the high priest's house, where all the chief priests, elders and scribes came together.
en.R: The men took Jesus to the house of the high priest. All the leading priests, the elders, and the teachers of God's law met together there.

es.L: Y llevaron a Jesús ante el sumo sacerdote, y se reúnen todos los jefes de los sacerdotes y los ancianos y los escribas.
es.B: Llevaron a Jesús a casa del sumo sacerdote, donde se reunieron todos los jefes de los sacerdotes, los ancianos y los escribas.
es.R: Los hombres llevaron a Jesús a la casa del sumo sacerdote. Allí se reunieron todos los jefes de los sacerdotes, los ancianos y los maestros de la ley.

sw.L: Na walimpeleka Yesu kwa kuhani mkuu, na wanakusanyika wakuu wote wa makuhani na wazee na waandishi.
sw.B: Walimpeleka Yesu nyumbani kwa kuhani mkuu, ambako wakuu wote wa makuhani, wazee na waandishi walikusanyika.
sw.R: Wale watu walimpeleka Yesu nyumbani kwa kuhani mkuu. Wakuu wote wa makuhani, wazee na walimu wa sheria wakakutana huko.

decisions.choice: the high priest: Caiaphas, high priest at this time
decisions.reason: Mark does not name him. Matthew 26:57 names Caiaphas, who held the office from about AD 18 to 36.

decisions.choice: all the chief priests, elders and scribes: the members of the council
decisions.reason: The three groups made up the council, the highest Jewish court in Jerusalem (14:55). They meet at night, in the high priest's house.

decisions.choice: come together: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: the house of the high priest
decisions.reason: Readable says where they took him, as 14:54 shows.

source.text: καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ ἕως ἔσω εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ ἦν συγκαθήμενος μετὰ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν καὶ θερμαινόμενος πρὸς τὸ φῶς.

records.literal_gloss: And Peter from a distance followed him as far as inside into the courtyard of the high priest, and he was sitting with the officers and warming himself at the light.

en.L: And Peter followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from a distance, right inside into the courtyard of the high priest, and he was sitting with the officers and warming himself at the fire.
en.B: Peter kept well back, but followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the way inside the high priest's courtyard. He sat down among the guards and warmed himself by the firelight.
en.R: Peter followed Jesus, but he stayed far behind. He went into the yard of the high priest's house. He sat with the guards and warmed himself by the fire.

es.L: Y Pedro {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió de lejos hasta dentro, al patio del sumo sacerdote, y estaba sentado con los guardias y calentándose junto a la lumbre.
es.B: Pedro se mantuvo a buena distancia, pero {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió hasta dentro del patio del sumo sacerdote. Se sentó entre los guardias y se calentaba a la luz del fuego.
es.R: Pedro siguió a Jesús, pero se quedó muy atrás. Entró en el patio de la casa del sumo sacerdote. Se sentó con los guardias y se calentaba junto al fuego.

sw.L: Na Petro alimfuata kwa mbali hadi ndani ya ua wa kuhani mkuu, naye alikuwa ameketi pamoja na walinzi akiota moto.
sw.B: Petro alikaa nyuma sana, lakini alimfuata mpaka ndani ya ua wa kuhani mkuu. Akaketi kati ya walinzi, akiota moto katika mwanga wake.
sw.R: Petro alimfuata Yesu, lakini alikaa nyuma sana. Aliingia uani mwa nyumba ya kuhani mkuu. Akaketi pamoja na walinzi, akaota moto.

decisions.choice: the light: the fire, whose light showed his face
decisions.reason: The word means light. Here it is a fire, and its light lets the servant girl see him (14:67).

decisions.choice: officers: attendants of the council, the temple guards
decisions.reason: The word means assistants or attendants; here they are the guards who served the high priest.

decisions.choice: courtyard: the open court inside a large house
decisions.reason: Large houses were built around an open court.

decisions.choice: los guardias
decisions.reason: Attendants of the council, the temple guards (meaning decision m2), as in Matthew 26:58. "Guardias" says what they were; "alguaciles" is old-fashioned and "criados" would make them household servants.

decisions.choice: walinzi
decisions.reason: Attendants of the council, the temple guards (meaning decision m2), as in Matthew 26:58. "Walinzi" says what they were; "watumishi" is kept for slaves.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ ὅλον τὸ συνέδριον ἐζήτουν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ μαρτυρίαν εἰς τὸ θανατῶσαι αὐτόν, καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον·

records.literal_gloss: And the chief priests and all the Council were seeking against Jesus testimony in order to put to death him, and not they were finding.

en.L: Now the chief priests and the whole Council were seeking testimony against Jesus in order to put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death, and they were not finding [any].
en.B: Meanwhile the chief priests and the entire Council searched for testimony against Jesus that would let them have {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} executed, but they could not find any.
en.R: The leading priests and the whole Jewish council tried to find people who would say something against Jesus. They wanted a reason to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But they could not find any.

es.L: Y los jefes de los sacerdotes y todo el concilio buscaban testimonio contra Jesús para darle muerte, y no [lo] encontraban.
es.B: Mientras tanto, los jefes de los sacerdotes y todo el Consejo buscaban algún testimonio contra Jesús que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevara a la muerte, pero no encontraban ninguno.
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y todo el Consejo Supremo de los judíos trataban de encontrar a alguien que dijera algo contra Jesús. Querían una razón para matarlo. Pero no encontraban ninguna.

sw.L: Na wakuu wa makuhani na baraza zima walikuwa wakitafuta ushahidi dhidi ya Yesu ili wamuue, wala hawakuupata.
sw.B: Wakati huo wakuu wa makuhani na baraza zima walikuwa wakitafuta ushahidi dhidi ya Yesu ili wapate kumhukumu kifo, lakini hawakupata wowote.
sw.R: Wakuu wa makuhani na baraza kuu lote la Wayahudi walijaribu kutafuta watu ambao wangesema jambo lolote dhidi ya Yesu. Walitaka sababu ya kumuua. Lakini hawakupata yoyote.

decisions.choice: the Council: the Sanhedrin, the highest Jewish court
decisions.reason: The council in Jerusalem had seventy-one members under the high priest and judged matters of Jewish law.

decisions.choice: testimony: the evidence of witnesses
decisions.reason: The law required the word of two or three witnesses for a sentence of death (Deuteronomy 17:6).

decisions.choice: they had decided on the end first
decisions.reason: Mark shows that they were looking for evidence to fit a verdict already reached (14:1).

decisions.choice: the whole Jewish council
decisions.reason: Readable says what the Council was, as in 15:1.

decisions.choice: el concilio (L); el Consejo (B); el Consejo Supremo de los judíos (R)
decisions.reason: The Sanhedrin, the highest Jewish court (meaning decision m1), with the words of Matthew 26:59. Readable says it was the highest Jewish court, as the English "the whole Jewish council" does.

decisions.choice: baraza (L, B); baraza kuu la Wayahudi (R)
decisions.reason: The Sanhedrin, the highest Jewish court (meaning decision m1), with the words of Matthew 26:59. Readable says it was the highest Jewish court, as the English "the whole Jewish council" does.

source.text: πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐψευδομαρτύρουν κατ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἴσαι αἱ μαρτυρίαι οὐκ ἦσαν.

records.literal_gloss: Many for were bearing false witness against him, and alike the testimonies not were.

en.L: For many were bearing false witness against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and their testimonies were not consistent.
en.B: Plenty of people testified falsely against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but what they said did not match.
en.R: Many people told lies about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But their stories did not agree with each other.

es.L: Porque muchos daban falso testimonio contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y los testimonios no concordaban.
es.B: Muchos declaraban en falso contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, pero sus declaraciones no coincidían.
es.R: Muchos dijeron mentiras contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Pero lo que contaban no coincidía.

sw.L: Kwa maana wengi walikuwa wakitoa ushahidi wa uongo dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na shuhuda zao hazikulingana.
sw.B: Watu wengi walitoa ushahidi wa uongo dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, lakini maneno yao hayakupatana.
sw.R: Watu wengi walisema uongo juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Lakini habari zao hazikukubaliana.

decisions.choice: not alike: not consistent, not agreeing
decisions.reason: Under the law two witnesses had to agree on the facts (Deuteronomy 19:15). These did not, so their word could not stand.

decisions.choice: false witnesses: an echo of the psalms of the righteous sufferer
decisions.reason: Psalm 27:12 and Psalm 35:11 speak of false witnesses rising up against the righteous.

source.text: καί τινες ἀναστάντες ἐψευδομαρτύρουν κατ’ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες ὅτι Ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ὅτι Ἐγὼ καταλύσω τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον τὸν χειροποίητον καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν ἄλλον ἀχειροποίητον οἰκοδομήσω·

records.literal_gloss: And some having stood up were bearing false witness against him saying \v 58 that We heard him saying that I will destroy the temple this the made with hands and in three days another not made with hands I will build.

en.L: And some stood up and were bearing false witness against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, \v 58 "We heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saying, 'I will destroy this temple made with hands, and in three days I will build another not made with hands.'"
en.B: Then some of them got up and brought a false charge against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: \v 58 "We heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} declare, 'I will pull down this temple that human hands have made, and in three days I will put up another that no hands have made.'"
en.R: Then some people stood up and told this lie about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: \v 58 "We heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} say, 'I will tear down this temple that people built. Then in three days I will build a different one, which people do not build.'"

es.L: Y algunos, levantándose, daban falso testimonio contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, diciendo: \v 58 «Nosotros {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oímos decir: “Yo destruiré este templo hecho con manos, y en tres días edificaré otro no hecho con manos”».
es.B: Entonces algunos se levantaron y presentaron contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} una acusación falsa: \v 58 «Nosotros {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oímos declarar: “Yo derribaré este templo hecho por manos humanas, y en tres días levantaré otro que no está hecho por manos humanas”».
es.R: Entonces algunos se pusieron de pie y dijeron esta mentira contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: \v 58 «Nosotros {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oímos decir: “Voy a destruir este templo que construyó la gente. Y en tres días construiré otro diferente, uno que no construye la gente”».

sw.L: Na baadhi, wakisimama, walikuwa wakitoa ushahidi wa uongo dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wakisema, \v 58 "Sisi tulimsikia akisema, 'Mimi nitalivunja hekalu hili lililojengwa kwa mikono, na kwa siku tatu nitajenga jingine lisilojengwa kwa mikono.'"
sw.B: Kisha baadhi yao walisimama, wakatoa shtaka la uongo dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}: \v 58 "Tulimsikia akisema, 'Nitalibomoa hekalu hili lililojengwa kwa mikono ya wanadamu, na kwa siku tatu nitajenga jingine lisilojengwa kwa mikono ya mtu.'"
sw.R: Kisha watu fulani walisimama, wakasema uongo huu juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}: \v 58 "Tulimsikia akisema, 'Nitaliharibu hekalu hili lililojengwa na watu. Kisha kwa siku tatu nitajenga jingine tofauti, lisilojengwa na watu.'"

decisions.choice: false witness: Jesus had not said he would destroy the temple
decisions.reason: Jesus foretold that the temple would be destroyed (13:2), but Mark calls this report false. John 2:19 has a saying about the temple of his body, which may lie behind it.

decisions.choice: made with hands; not made with hands: human-made and made by God
alternatives: built of stone; built of wood
decisions.reason: "Made with hands" was often said of idols and of things that are only human (Acts 7:48). A temple not made with hands would be God's own work.

decisions.choice: another temple: a new place of God's presence
decisions.reason: Mark does not explain it. Christians later saw in it Jesus' risen body or the community of his people, but Mark leaves it as the witnesses' charge.

decisions.choice: temple: the sanctuary itself
decisions.reason: The word here is the one for the sanctuary building, not the whole temple area of 14:49.

source.text: καὶ οὐδὲ οὕτως ἴση ἦν ἡ μαρτυρία αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And not even thus alike was the testimony of them.

en.L: And even so their testimony was not consistent.
en.B: But even on this point what they said did not match.
en.R: But even these people did not tell the same story.

es.L: Y ni aun así concordaba su testimonio.
es.B: Pero ni siquiera en este punto coincidían sus declaraciones.
es.R: Pero ni siquiera estas personas contaban lo mismo.

sw.L: Wala hata hivyo ushahidi wao haukulingana.
sw.B: Lakini hata katika jambo hili maneno yao hayakupatana.
sw.R: Lakini hata watu hao hawakusema habari moja.

decisions.choice: not even thus: not even on this charge
decisions.reason: Even the temple saying could not be used, because the witnesses did not agree.

source.text: καὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἰς μέσον ἐπηρώτησεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν λέγων· Οὐκ ἀποκρίνῃ οὐδέν;

records.literal_gloss: And having stood up the high priest in the middle questioned Jesus saying, Not you answer nothing?

en.L: And the high priest stood up in the middle and questioned Jesus, saying, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} answer nothing?
en.B: The high priest rose, stepped into the middle and put a question to Jesus: "Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} no answer at all?
en.R: Then the high priest stood up in front of everyone. He asked Jesus, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not going to answer?

es.L: Y levantándose el sumo sacerdote en medio, interrogó a Jesús, diciendo: «¿No respondes nada?
es.B: El sumo sacerdote se levantó, pasó al centro y le preguntó a Jesús: «¿No tienes ninguna respuesta?
es.R: Entonces el sumo sacerdote se puso de pie delante de todos. Le preguntó a Jesús: «¿No vas a responder?

sw.L: Na kuhani mkuu, akisimama katikati, alimwuliza Yesu, akisema, "Hujibu chochote?
sw.B: Kuhani mkuu aliinuka, akasimama katikati, akamwuliza Yesu, "Huna jibu lolote?
sw.R: Kisha kuhani mkuu alisimama mbele ya wote. Akamwuliza Yesu, "Je, hutajibu?

decisions.choice: two questions: Do you answer nothing? What are these testifying against you?
alternatives: one question: Do you answer nothing to what these testify against you?
decisions.reason: The words can be read as one question or two. The SBLGNT makes them two sentences.

decisions.choice: in the middle: in the center of the council
alternatives: in the middle of the night
decisions.reason: The council sat in a half circle; the high priest steps forward to question the accused.

source.text: τί οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;

records.literal_gloss: What these you testify against?

en.L: What are these testifying against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"
en.B: What is this that these people are saying against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"
en.R: What about all these things they are saying against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

es.L: ¿Qué testifican estos contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?».
es.B: ¿Qué es esto que dicen estos contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?».
es.R: ¿Qué dices de todas estas cosas que dicen contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?».

sw.L: Hawa wanashuhudia nini dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}?"
sw.B: Ni nini hiki ambacho watu hawa wanasema dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}?"
sw.R: Unasemaje kuhusu mambo haya yote wanayosema dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}?"

decisions.choice: what are these testifying: what do you say to their charges?
alternatives: what are they saying (he did not hear)
decisions.reason: The high priest asks Jesus to answer the charges.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἐσιώπα καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίνατο οὐδέν.

records.literal_gloss: But he was silent and not answered nothing.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was silent and answered nothing.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept silent and made no answer at all.
en.R: But Jesus said nothing. He did not answer at all.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} callaba y no respondió nada.
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} guardó silencio y no dio ninguna respuesta.
es.R: Pero Jesús no dijo nada. No respondió ni una palabra.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alinyamaza, wala hakujibu neno.
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikaa kimya, wala hakutoa jibu lolote.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu hakusema kitu. Hakujibu hata neno moja.

decisions.choice: he was silent: an echo of Isaiah 53:7
decisions.reason: The servant of the LORD was led like a lamb to slaughter and did not open his mouth.

decisions.choice: not ... nothing: not a word
decisions.reason: The double negative makes the silence complete.

source.text: πάλιν ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ εὐλογητοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: Again the high priest was questioning him and says to him, You are the Christ the Son of the Blessed?

en.L: Again the high priest was questioning {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of the Blessed [One]?"
en.B: Again the high priest put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the Son of the Blessed One?"
en.R: The high priest asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the Son of God, the Blessed One?"

es.L: De nuevo el sumo sacerdote {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} interrogaba y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice: «¿Tú eres el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Hijo del Bendito?».
es.B: De nuevo el sumo sacerdote {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Hijo del Bendito?».
es.R: El sumo sacerdote {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} volvió a preguntar: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Hijo de Dios, el Bendito?».

sw.L: Tena kuhani mkuu alikuwa akimwuliza, naye anamwambia, "Wewe ndiwe {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mwana wa Yule Anayehimidiwa?"
sw.B: Kuhani mkuu akamwuliza tena, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mwana wa Yule Anayehimidiwa?"
sw.R: Kuhani mkuu akamwuliza tena, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mwana wa Mungu, Yule Anayehimidiwa?"

decisions.choice: the Blessed: God
decisions.reason: Jews spoke of God with titles like "the Blessed One" out of reverence for his name.

decisions.choice: the Christ, the Son of the Blessed: the anointed king, God's Son
decisions.reason: The two titles name one figure. The king from David's line was called God's son (2 Samuel 7:14; Psalm 2:7). Mark opened his book with both titles (1:1).

decisions.choice: You: emphatic
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed: you, this prisoner, the Messiah?

decisions.choice: the Son of God, the Blessed One
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom the title means.

decisions.choice: el Cristo|el Mesías, with "el" outside the christos span, at every level
alternatives: Cristo|el Mesías, as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: The Greek has the article, and Spanish needs it before the title in both readings, so the article stands outside the span at every level, as the term sheet sets for "el Cristo" used as a title.

decisions.choice: Yule Anayehimidiwa
decisions.reason: A reverent way of naming God (meaning decision m1), the one whom people bless and praise. "Anayehimidiwa" says that; "mbarikiwa" reads as someone who has received a blessing.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι, καὶ ὄψεσθε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ δεξιῶν καθήμενον τῆς δυνάμεως καὶ ἐρχόμενον μετὰ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus said, I am, and you will see the Son of Man at the right [hand] sitting of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.

en.L: And Jesus said, "I am, and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven."
en.B: Jesus said, "I am. And you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power, and coming with the clouds of heaven."
en.R: Jesus said, "Yes, I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right side of God, the Mighty One. You will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} coming with the clouds of heaven."

es.L: Y Jesús dijo: «Yo soy, y {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} al Hijo del Hombre sentado a [la] derecha del Poder y viniendo con las nubes del cielo».
es.B: Jesús respondió: «Yo soy. Y {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} al Hijo del Hombre sentado a la derecha del Poder, y viniendo con las nubes del cielo».
es.R: Jesús dijo: «Sí, yo soy. Y {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} al Hijo del Hombre sentado a la derecha de Dios, el Todopoderoso. También {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} venir con las nubes del cielo».

sw.L: Naye Yesu akasema, "Ndimi; nanyi mtamwona Mwana wa Adamu akiketi upande wa kulia wa Uweza na akija pamoja na mawingu ya mbinguni."
sw.B: Yesu akasema, "Mimi ndiye. Nanyi mtamwona Mwana wa Adamu ameketi upande wa kulia wa Uweza, akija pamoja na mawingu ya mbinguni."
sw.R: Yesu akasema, "Ndiyo, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndiye. Nanyi mtamwona Mwana wa Adamu ameketi upande wa kulia wa Mungu, Mwenye Uweza. Tena mtamwona akija pamoja na mawingu ya mbinguni."

decisions.choice: I am: yes, I am the Messiah, the Son of God
alternatives: only the divine name of Exodus 3:14
decisions.reason: The words answer the question directly. Some hear an echo of God's name, as at 6:50, but the plain sense is yes.

decisions.choice: I am, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "You say that I am", which is like Matthew 26:64 and Luke 22:70. Nearly all have "I am". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the right hand of the Power; coming with the clouds: Psalm 110:1 and Daniel 7:13
decisions.reason: Psalm 110:1 has the Lord tell the king to sit at his right hand; Daniel 7:13 sees one like a son of man coming with the clouds to God. Jesus joins them, as he did in 12:36 and 13:26. In the Psalm the Hebrew has the divine name, the LORD.

decisions.choice: the Power: God
decisions.reason: Another reverent title for God, like "the Blessed One" in 14:61.

decisions.choice: God, the Mighty One; You will see him
decisions.reason: Readable names God, adds "yes" to make the answer plain, and splits the long sentence in two.

decisions.choice: Uweza (L, B); Mungu, Mwenye Uweza (R)
decisions.reason: "The Power" is a reverent way of naming God (meaning decision m4), rendered as at Matthew 26:64: "Uweza" is might as belonging to God and reads as a name; "Nguvu" is everyday strength. Readable names God, as the English does.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀρχιερεὺς διαρρήξας τοὺς χιτῶνας αὐτοῦ λέγει· Τί ἔτι χρείαν ἔχομεν μαρτύρων;

records.literal_gloss: And the high priest having torn the tunics of him says, What still need have we of witnesses?

en.L: And the high priest, tearing his garments, says, "What further need do we have of witnesses?
en.B: The high priest ripped his clothes. "What more do we need witnesses for?
en.R: The high priest tore his clothes to show his horror. He said, "We do not need any more witnesses!

es.L: Y el sumo sacerdote, rasgando sus túnicas, dice: «¿Qué necesidad tenemos todavía de testigos?
es.B: El sumo sacerdote se rasgó la ropa: «¿Para qué necesitamos más testigos?
es.R: El sumo sacerdote se rasgó la ropa para mostrar su horror. Dijo: «¡No necesitamos más testigos!

sw.L: Naye kuhani mkuu, akiyararua mavazi yake, anasema, "Tuna haja gani tena ya mashahidi?
sw.B: Kuhani mkuu alirarua nguo zake. "Tunahitaji mashahidi zaidi kwa ajili ya nini?
sw.R: Kuhani mkuu alirarua nguo zake kuonyesha jinsi alivyoshtuka. Akasema, "Hatuhitaji mashahidi wengine!

decisions.choice: tearing his garments: a sign of horror at hearing blasphemy
decisions.reason: Tearing clothes showed grief or horror (2 Kings 18:37). Later Jewish rules say judges did this on hearing blasphemy.

decisions.choice: garments: tunics, the clothes worn under the cloak
alternatives: the high priest's robes of office
decisions.reason: The word is plural; men of rank might wear two tunics.

decisions.choice: to show his horror
decisions.reason: Readable explains the act.

source.text: ἠκούσατε τῆς βλασφημίας· τί ὑμῖν φαίνεται;

records.literal_gloss: You heard the blasphemy; what to you does it appear?

en.L: You have heard the blasphemy. What does it seem to you?"
en.B: You heard the blasphemy for yourselves. What is your verdict?"
en.R: You heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} say this terrible thing against God. What do you think we should do?"

es.L: {{plural_you:Han oído|Habéis oído}} la blasfemia. ¿Qué {{plural_you:les|os}} parece?».
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes mismos han oído|Vosotros mismos habéis oído}} la blasfemia. ¿Cuál es {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} veredicto?».
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} decir esta cosa terrible contra Dios. ¿Qué {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} que debemos hacer?».

sw.L: Mmesikia kufuru hiyo. Mnaonaje?"
sw.B: Ninyi wenyewe mmesikia kufuru hiyo. Hukumu yenu ni nini?"
sw.R: Mmemsikia akisema neno hili baya dhidi ya Mungu. Mnafikiri tufanye nini?"

decisions.choice: blasphemy: speech that insults God or claims what belongs to God
decisions.reason: The law punished one who cursed God's name (Leviticus 24:16). Mark does not say what made Jesus' words blasphemy. Most likely it was his claim to sit at God's right hand.

decisions.choice: what does it seem to you?: what is your judgment?
decisions.reason: The high priest asks the council for its verdict.

decisions.choice: say this terrible thing against God
decisions.reason: Readable says what blasphemy is.

source.text: οἱ δὲ πάντες κατέκριναν αὐτὸν ἔνοχον εἶναι θανάτου.

records.literal_gloss: And all condemned him to be deserving of death.

en.L: And they all condemned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as deserving death.
en.B: Every one of them condemned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} deserved to die.
en.R: All of them said that Jesus was guilty and should be put to death.

es.L: Y todos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} condenaron como reo de muerte.
es.B: Todos ellos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} condenaron: merecía morir.
es.R: Todos dijeron que Jesús era culpable y que debía morir.

sw.L: Nao wote walimhukumu kuwa anastahili kifo.
sw.B: Wote walimhukumu: alistahili kufa.
sw.R: Wote walisema kwamba Yesu ana hatia na anapaswa kuuawa.

decisions.choice: deserving of death: liable to the death penalty
decisions.reason: They judge him guilty of a crime that carries death. The council then hands him to Pilate (15:1), since the Romans kept the power to execute.

decisions.choice: all: all who were present
alternatives: every member of the council without exception
decisions.reason: Mark says all, but Joseph of Arimathea, a council member, was waiting for God's kingdom (15:43). Luke 23:51 says he had not agreed with their decision.

source.text: καὶ ἤρξαντό τινες ἐμπτύειν αὐτῷ καὶ περικαλύπτειν αὐτοῦ τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ κολαφίζειν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγειν αὐτῷ· Προφήτευσον, καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ῥαπίσμασιν αὐτὸν ἔλαβον.

records.literal_gloss: And began some to spit on him and to cover of him the face and to strike him and to say to him, Prophesy, and the officers with slaps him received.

en.L: And some began to spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and to cover {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face and to strike {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with fists and to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Prophesy!" And the officers received {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with slaps.
en.B: Some of them started spitting on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They covered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face, punched {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and taunted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Prophesy!" The guards, too, took charge of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and struck {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with open hands.
en.R: Then some people began to spit on Jesus. They covered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could not see. They hit {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with their fists and said, "Prophesy! Show us you are a prophet!" Then the guards took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and slapped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y algunos comenzaron a escupirle y a cubrir {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} rostro y a darle puñetazos y a decirle: «¡Profetiza!». Y los guardias {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} recibieron a bofetadas.
es.B: Algunos de ellos empezaron a escupirle. {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} cubrieron la cara, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dieron puñetazos y se burlaban de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: «¡Profetiza!». También los guardias se hicieron cargo de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} abofetearon.
es.R: Entonces algunos comenzaron a escupir a Jesús. Le taparon la cara para que no pudiera ver, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} golpearon con los puños y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} decían: «¡Profetiza! ¡Demuestra que eres profeta!». Después los guardias se {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dieron bofetadas.

sw.L: Na baadhi walianza kumtemea mate na kuufunika uso {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na kumpiga ngumi na kumwambia, "Tabiri!" Na walinzi walimpokea kwa makofi.
sw.B: Baadhi yao walianza kumtemea mate. Wakaufunika uso {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, wakampiga ngumi, wakamdhihaki, "Tabiri!" Walinzi nao wakamchukua, wakampiga makofi.
sw.R: Kisha watu fulani walianza kumtemea Yesu mate. Wakaufunika uso {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ili asiweze kuona. Wakampiga ngumi, wakasema, "Tabiri! Tuonyeshe kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni nabii!" Kisha walinzi walimchukua, wakampiga makofi.

decisions.choice: Prophesy!: a mocking test, while his own prophecy comes true
decisions.reason: With his face covered, they dare him to name who struck him (Luke 22:64). At that very hour Peter is fulfilling Jesus' prophecy of 14:30 in the courtyard below.

decisions.choice: spitting and striking: an echo of Isaiah 50:6
decisions.reason: The servant says, "I did not hide my face from shame and spitting." Jesus foretold this in 10:34.

decisions.choice: received him with slaps: took him and beat him
decisions.reason: The phrase means they took charge of him with blows.

decisions.choice: received, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts have verbs meaning they struck or threw him. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: so that he could not see; Show us you are a prophet
decisions.reason: Readable explains the point of the covering and of the taunt.

source.text: Καὶ ὄντος τοῦ Πέτρου κάτω ἐν τῇ αὐλῇ ἔρχεται μία τῶν παιδισκῶν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, καὶ ἰδοῦσα τὸν Πέτρον θερμαινόμενον ἐμβλέψασα αὐτῷ λέγει· Καὶ σὺ μετὰ τοῦ Ναζαρηνοῦ ἦσθα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And being Peter below in the courtyard comes one of the servant girls of the high priest, \v 67 and having seen Peter warming himself, having looked at him she says, And you with the Nazarene were, Jesus.

en.L: And while Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high priest comes, \v 67 and seeing Peter warming himself, she looks at him and says, "You too were with the Nazarene, Jesus."
en.B: Meanwhile Peter was below in the courtyard. One of the high priest's servant girls came along, \v 67 and when she noticed Peter warming himself, she studied his face and said, "You, too, were with the man from Nazareth, Jesus."
en.R: Peter was still down in the yard. A young woman who served the high priest came there. \v 67 She saw Peter warming himself by the fire. She looked closely at him and said, "You were with Jesus, the man from Nazareth."

es.L: Y estando Pedro abajo en el patio, viene una de las criadas del sumo sacerdote, \v 67 y viendo a Pedro que se calentaba, mirándolo fijamente, dice: «También tú estabas con el Nazareno, Jesús».
es.B: Mientras tanto, Pedro estaba abajo, en el patio. Llegó una de las criadas del sumo sacerdote \v 67 y, al ver a Pedro calentándose, lo miró fijamente y le dijo: «Tú también estabas con el hombre de Nazaret, con Jesús».
es.R: Pedro todavía estaba abajo, en el patio. Llegó allí una muchacha que trabajaba para el sumo sacerdote. \v 67 Vio a Pedro calentándose junto al fuego. Lo miró bien y le dijo: «Tú estabas con Jesús, el hombre de Nazaret».

sw.L: Na Petro alipokuwa chini uani, anakuja mmoja wa vijakazi wa kuhani mkuu, \v 67 na alipomwona Petro akiota moto, akimkazia macho, anasema, "Wewe pia ulikuwa pamoja na yule Mnazareti, Yesu."
sw.B: Wakati huo Petro alikuwa chini uani. Mmoja wa watumishi wa kike wa kuhani mkuu alikuja, \v 67 na alipomwona Petro akiota moto, alimkazia macho, akasema, "Wewe pia ulikuwa pamoja na yule mtu wa Nazareti, Yesu."
sw.R: Petro alikuwa bado chini uani. Msichana mmoja aliyemtumikia kuhani mkuu alifika pale. \v 67 Alimwona Petro akiota moto. Akamtazama sana, akasema, "Wewe ulikuwa pamoja na Yesu, yule mtu wa Nazareti."

decisions.choice: servant girl: a young female slave or servant of the household
decisions.reason: The word was used of a young woman who served in a house, often a slave. Such a girl kept the door (John 18:16-17).

decisions.choice: below: the council met in a room above the courtyard
decisions.reason: Mark pictures the hearing upstairs while Peter waits in the courtyard below.

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: the man from Nazareth
decisions.reason: The name says where Jesus came from (1:9, 1:24). In her mouth it may sound scornful of a man from a small Galilean village.

decisions.choice: having looked at him: she looked hard at him
decisions.reason: The verb means to fix one's eyes on someone.

decisions.choice: una de las criadas (L, B); una muchacha que trabajaba para el sumo sacerdote (R); also 14:69
decisions.reason: A young woman serving in the household, slave or servant (meaning decision m1), as at Matthew 26:69. Readable says it in plain words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: el Nazareno (L); el hombre de Nazaret (B, R)
decisions.reason: The man from Nazareth (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the single word, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: kijakazi (L); mtumishi wa kike (B); msichana aliyemtumikia kuhani mkuu (R); also 14:69
decisions.reason: A young female slave or servant of the household (meaning decision m1), as at Matthew 26:69. Readable says it in plain words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Mnazareti (L); mtu wa Nazareti (B, R)
decisions.reason: The man from Nazareth (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the single word, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο λέγων· Οὔτε οἶδα οὔτε ἐπίσταμαι σὺ τί λέγεις, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω εἰς τὸ προαύλιον καὶ ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν.

records.literal_gloss: But he denied saying, Neither I know nor understand you what say. And he went out outside into the forecourt; and a rooster crowed.

en.L: But he denied [it], saying, "I neither know nor understand what you are saying." And he went outside into the forecourt, and a rooster crowed.
en.B: But Peter denied it: "I have no idea what you are talking about; I do not understand you." Then he went out to the entrance, and a rooster crowed.
en.R: But Peter said that was not true. He said, "I do not know what you are talking about. I do not understand you." Then Peter went out to the entrance of the yard. Just then a rooster crowed.

es.L: Pero él [lo] negó, diciendo: «Ni sé ni entiendo qué dices tú». Y salió afuera, al vestíbulo, y un gallo cantó.
es.B: Pero Pedro lo negó: «No tengo idea de qué hablas; no te entiendo». Luego salió hacia la entrada, y un gallo cantó.
