es.R: Pero Pedro dijo que no era cierto: «No sé de qué estás hablando. No te entiendo». Luego Pedro salió hacia la entrada del patio. En ese momento cantó un gallo.

sw.L: Lakini yeye alikana, akisema, "Sijui wala sielewi wewe unachosema." Naye akatoka nje mpaka ukumbi wa mbele, na jogoo akawika.
sw.B: Lakini Petro alikana: "Sijui hata unachozungumzia; sikuelewi." Kisha akatoka nje kwenda kwenye lango, na jogoo akawika.
sw.R: Lakini Petro alisema si kweli. Akasema, "Sijui unachozungumza. Sikuelewi." Kisha Petro akatoka akaenda kwenye lango la ua. Wakati huo huo jogoo aliwika.

decisions.choice: and a rooster crowed, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some important early manuscripts do not have these words. They fit Jesus' words about a rooster crowing twice (14:30, 14:72), which those manuscripts also lack in part. The SBLGNT includes them. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: I neither know nor understand what you are saying
alternatives: I neither know nor understand. What are you saying?
decisions.reason: The words can be split into a denial and a question. Either way Peter pretends not to understand her.

decisions.choice: forecourt: the entrance passage or gateway into the courtyard
alternatives: a porch at the front of the house
decisions.reason: The word means the area in front of the courtyard, the gateway. Peter moves away from the light of the fire.

decisions.choice: denied: said it was not so
decisions.reason: This is the first of the three denials Jesus foretold in 14:30.

decisions.choice: el vestíbulo (L); la entrada (B); la entrada del patio (R)
decisions.reason: The entrance passage or gateway into the courtyard (meaning decision m3). "Vestíbulo" is the space just inside a building's door, close to the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "entrada", as the English does.

decisions.choice: ukumbi wa mbele (L); lango (B); lango la ua (R)
decisions.reason: The entrance passage or gateway into the courtyard (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the picture of a forecourt; Balanced and Readable say "lango" (gateway), as the English says "entrance".

source.text: καὶ ἡ παιδίσκη ἰδοῦσα αὐτὸν ἤρξατο πάλιν λέγειν τοῖς παρεστῶσιν ὅτι Οὗτος ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: And the servant girl having seen him began again to say to those standing by that This [one] of them is.

en.L: And the servant girl, seeing him, began again to say to those standing by, "This [man] is one of them."
en.B: The servant girl caught sight of him there and started saying again to the people standing around, "He is one of them."
en.R: The servant girl saw him there. She began to tell the people standing around, "This man is one of Jesus' followers!"

es.L: Y la criada, al verlo, comenzó otra vez a decir a los que estaban allí: «Este es de ellos».
es.B: La criada lo vio allí y volvió a decir a los que estaban alrededor: «Este es uno de ellos».
es.R: La criada lo vio allí. Comenzó a decirles a los que estaban alrededor: «¡Este hombre es uno de los discípulos de Jesús!».

sw.L: Na kijakazi yule, alipomwona, alianza tena kuwaambia wale waliosimama karibu, "Huyu ni mmoja wao."
sw.B: Yule mtumishi wa kike alimwona pale, akaanza tena kuwaambia watu waliosimama karibu, "Huyu ni mmoja wao."
sw.R: Yule msichana alimwona pale. Akaanza kuwaambia watu waliosimama pale, "Mtu huyu ni mmoja wa wanafunzi wa Yesu!"

decisions.choice: the servant girl: the same girl as in 14:66
decisions.reason: The article points back to the girl already named. Matthew 26:71 speaks of another girl; the Gospels tell the scene in slightly different ways.

decisions.choice: one of them: one of Jesus' followers
decisions.reason: She tells the bystanders that Peter belongs to Jesus' band.

decisions.choice: one of Jesus' followers
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" are.

source.text: ὁ δὲ πάλιν ἠρνεῖτο.

records.literal_gloss: But again he was denying.

en.L: But again he denied [it].
en.B: Again he denied it.
en.R: Again Peter said it was not true.

es.L: Pero él de nuevo [lo] negaba.
es.B: Él volvió a negarlo.
es.R: Otra vez Pedro dijo que no era cierto.

sw.L: Lakini yeye alikuwa akikana tena.
sw.B: Akakana tena.
sw.R: Petro akasema tena kwamba si kweli.

decisions.choice: he was denying: he kept denying
decisions.reason: The tense may show that he denied it more than once to those standing by. This is the second denial.

source.text: καὶ μετὰ μικρὸν πάλιν οἱ παρεστῶτες ἔλεγον τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ἀληθῶς ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ, καὶ γὰρ Γαλιλαῖος εἶ καὶ ἡ λαλιά σου ὁμοιάζει·

records.literal_gloss: And after a little again those standing by were saying to Peter, Truly of them you are, also for a Galilean you are, and the speech of you is like.

en.L: And after a little while, again those standing by were saying to Peter, "Truly you are [one] of them, for you are also a Galilean, and your speech is like [theirs]."
en.B: A little later the bystanders again said to Peter, "You really are one of them. You are from Galilee, after all; the way you talk gives you away."
en.R: A little while later, the people standing there said to Peter again, "You really are one of Jesus' followers. You are from Galilee, and you talk like people from there."

es.L: Y poco después, de nuevo los que estaban allí decían a Pedro: «Verdaderamente eres de ellos, pues también eres galileo, y tu manera de hablar se parece [a la suya]».
es.B: Poco después, los que estaban allí volvieron a decirle a Pedro: «Seguro que eres uno de ellos. Al fin y al cabo, eres galileo; tu manera de hablar te delata».
es.R: Un poco más tarde, los que estaban allí le dijeron otra vez a Pedro: «De verdad eres uno de los discípulos de Jesús. Eres de Galilea, y hablas como la gente de allí».

sw.L: Na baada ya kitambo, tena wale waliosimama karibu walikuwa wakimwambia Petro, "Kweli wewe ni mmoja wao, kwa maana wewe pia ni Mgalilaya, na usemi wako unafanana [na wao]."
sw.B: Muda mfupi baadaye, wale waliokuwa wamesimama pale walimwambia Petro tena, "Hakika wewe ni mmoja wao. Wewe ni Mgalilaya, na lafudhi yako inakutambulisha."
sw.R: Baadaye kidogo, watu waliosimama pale walimwambia Petro tena, "Kweli wewe ni mmoja wa wanafunzi wa Yesu. Wewe ni wa Galilaya, na unasema kama watu wa huko."

decisions.choice: a Galilean: Peter's accent marked him as from Galilee
decisions.reason: People from Galilee spoke with an accent that people in Judea could hear. Jesus and his followers were known as Galileans.

decisions.choice: and your speech is like [theirs], the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts do not have these words, which are like Matthew 26:73. The SBLGNT text includes them. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: truly: really, certainly
decisions.reason: The adverb means "surely". It is not the "amen" of Jesus' sayings.

decisions.choice: the way you talk gives you away
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense: his speech shows where he is from.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἤρξατο ἀναθεματίζειν καὶ ὀμνύναι ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦτον ὃν λέγετε.

records.literal_gloss: But he began to curse and to swear that Not I know the man this whom you speak of.

en.L: But he began to curse and to swear, "I do not know this man of whom you speak."
en.B: Then he started calling curses down and swearing oaths: "This man you speak of, I do not know him."
en.R: Then Peter said, "May God curse me if I am lying! I promise you, I do not know this man you are talking about!"

es.L: Pero él comenzó a lanzar maldiciones y a jurar: «No conozco a este hombre de quien {{plural_you:hablan|habláis}}».
es.B: Entonces comenzó a maldecir y a jurar: «A ese hombre del que {{plural_you:hablan|habláis}}, no lo conozco».
es.R: Entonces Pedro dijo: «¡Que Dios me maldiga si estoy mintiendo! {{plural_you:Les|Os}} juro que no conozco a ese hombre del que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} hablando».

sw.L: Lakini yeye alianza kulaani na kuapa, "Simjui mtu huyu mnayemsema."
sw.B: Ndipo alianza kulaani na kuapa: "Mtu huyu mnayemzungumzia, simjui."
sw.R: Kisha Petro akasema, "Mungu anilaani kama ninasema uongo! Nawaapia, simjui mtu huyu mnayemzungumzia!"

decisions.choice: curse: call down a curse, most likely on himself if he lies
decisions.reason: The verb means to put under a curse. Mark gives no object. It may mean Peter called a curse on himself, or even that he cursed Jesus. The first fits the oath that follows.

decisions.choice: swear: take an oath
decisions.reason: To swear was to call God as witness that one was telling the truth.

decisions.choice: this man: Peter will not even say his name
decisions.reason: Peter calls Jesus only "this man". This is the third denial.

decisions.choice: May God curse me if I am lying! I promise you
alternatives: he began to curse and to swear
decisions.reason: Readable puts the curse and the oath into words. Taking the curse as on himself follows the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: lanzar maldiciones (L); maldecir (B)
decisions.reason: Peter most likely called a curse down on himself if he was lying, but this is uncertain (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced say he cursed without naming on whom, as the English does; Readable spells out the likely sense, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: kulaani (L, B)
decisions.reason: Peter most likely called a curse down on himself if he was lying, but this is uncertain (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced say he cursed without naming on whom, as the English does; Readable spells out the likely sense, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκ δευτέρου ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν· καὶ ἀνεμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τὸ ῥῆμα ὡς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι δὶς τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ, καὶ ἐπιβαλὼν ἔκλαιεν.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately for a second [time] a rooster crowed. And remembered Peter the word as said to him Jesus that Before a rooster crows twice three times me you will deny; and having thrown upon he was weeping.

en.L: And immediately a rooster crowed a second time. And Peter remembered the word, how Jesus had said to him, "Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times." And breaking down, he was weeping.
en.B: At that moment a rooster crowed for the second time. Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: "Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times." Then Peter broke down in tears.
en.R: Right then the rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: "Before the rooster crows two times, you will say three times that you do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." Then Peter broke down and cried.

es.L: Y en seguida un gallo cantó por segunda vez. Y Pedro recordó la palabra, cómo Jesús le había dicho: «Antes que un gallo cante dos veces, tres veces {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} negarás». Y derrumbándose, lloraba.
es.B: En ese momento un gallo cantó por segunda vez. Pedro se acordó de lo que Jesús le había dicho: «Antes de que un gallo cante dos veces, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} negarás tres veces». Y Pedro rompió a llorar.
es.R: En ese mismo momento el gallo cantó por segunda vez. Pedro se acordó de lo que Jesús le había dicho: «Antes de que el gallo cante dos veces, dirás tres veces que no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conoces». Entonces Pedro se derrumbó y lloró.

sw.L: Na mara jogoo aliwika mara ya pili. Na Petro alikumbuka lile neno, jinsi Yesu alivyomwambia, "Kabla jogoo hajawika mara mbili, utanikana mara tatu." Naye akivunjika moyo, alikuwa akilia.
sw.B: Papo hapo jogoo aliwika mara ya pili. Petro akayakumbuka maneno ambayo Yesu alikuwa amemwambia: "Kabla jogoo hajawika mara mbili, utanikana mara tatu." Basi Petro akaangua kilio.
sw.R: Wakati huo huo jogoo aliwika mara ya pili. Petro akakumbuka jinsi Yesu alivyomwambia: "Kabla jogoo hajawika mara mbili, utasema mara tatu kwamba hunijui." Ndipo Petro akavunjika moyo, akalia.

decisions.choice: having thrown upon: he broke down, he burst into tears
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw upon, and its sense here is uncertain. It may mean he set himself to weeping or broke down; or that he thought about it, as some early translations took it; or that he threw his cloak over his head. All agree that Peter wept bitterly at what he had done.

decisions.choice: he was weeping: he wept and went on weeping
decisions.reason: The tense shows weeping that went on.

decisions.choice: immediately ... a second time, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "immediately", and some important early manuscripts lack "a second time" here and "twice" in the saying, as at 14:30 and 14:68. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus' word is fulfilled
decisions.reason: Everything Jesus said in 14:30 has come true, as his words about the cup and the scattering are coming true.

decisions.choice: broke down in tears (B); broke down and cried (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the most likely sense; the footnote gives the others.
